Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether environmental and social impacts of connectivity projects are being assessed, if so, 
the details thereof and safeguards implemented to ensure sustainable development; 
 
(b) whether the Government has evaluated economic benefits of improved Panchayat-city 
connectivity, if so, the findings thereof and the impact on employment, trade and rural 
development; 
 
(c) whether timelines have been fixed for completion of ongoing connectivity projects, if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons for delays affecting rural-urban integration; 
 
(d) whether grievance redressal mechanisms exist for issues related to connectivity projects, if 
so, the details thereof and the steps taken to ensure accountability and transparency; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to launch new initiatives to strengthen Panchayat to city 
connectivity, if so, the details thereof including funding, scope and expected outcomes? 
  
  
 ANSWER 
  
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH) 
  
(a) and (b): No, Sir. Ministry of Panchyati Raj does not implement any connectivity projects 
including Panchayat-city connectivity. 
  
However, Ministry of Rural Development has informed that Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana 
(PMGSY) was launched as a one-time special intervention to provide rural connectivity, by way 
of a single all-weather road for uplifting the socio- economic condition of the rural population. 
Subsequently, new interventions/ verticals namely PMGSY-II and PMGSY-III were added under 
the ambit of PMGSY for upgradation of the existing rural roads and for consolidation of through 
Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations. Further, in September 2024 Government 
has launched PMGSY-IV with the aim to provide all-weather road connectivity to 25,000 

2 
 
unconnected habitations of designated population size. New road projects are currently 
sanctioned under this scheme for the eligible habitations surveyed by the States and on 
submission of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the same. 
  
Ministry of Rural Development has further informed that various independent evaluation 
studies on PMGSY by NITI Aayog, World Bank etc. have concluded that rural roads 
constructed under PMGSY have improved access to education and health care facilities, 
facilitated employment generation in both farm and non-farm sectors, helped farmers in getting 
better farm prices, etc. through which there has been a rapid socio-economic transformation in 
rural areas. It has provided a long-term and sustained boost in the living standards of rural 
population living in the connected habitations. 
  
(c) and (d): Ministry of Rural Development has informed that in order to ensure progress in 
development outcomes, the Ministry is coordinating closely with the State Governments and 
providing the required assistance for early submission of DPRs. Department of Rural 
Development has organized Rashtriya Gramin Vikas Sammelan in the month of June 2026 in 
which PMGSY has been a topic of detailed discussion with States/UTs in the presence of all 
stakeholders. In addition, Regional Review Meetings and Monthly Meetings are also held 
routinely, so as to take stock of the progress and resolve any issues in the implementation 
process. 
  
(e) No, Sir. No new initiative is proposed by this Ministry to strengthen panchayat to city 
connectivity.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
(a) to (e) The Government regularly engages with Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), 
industry associations, State Governments and other stakeholders to identify sector-
specific opportunities, address trade-related issues and formulate strategies for 
enhancing India's exports. 
Tamil Nadu, being one of the country's leading exporting States, has significant export 
potential in sectors such as textiles and garments, leather and footwear, engineering 
goods, automobiles and auto components, electronics, marine products and MSMEs. 
Under the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative, all districts in the State have 
identified products and services with export potential. The State/UT and district-wise 

2 
 
list of products/services identified under the DEH initiative including districts of Tamil 
Nadu is placed at 
https://content.dgft.gov.in/Website/dgftprod/a667478a-d204-4d95-a71c 
a58452e1c6d9/Note%20-%20Districts%20as%20Export%20Hubs%20Initiative.pdf.  
Further, the recently launched Export Promotion Mission (EPM) aims to enhance 
India's export competitiveness through targeted interventions in areas such as export 
credit, logistics, infrastructure, market access, quality and standards, e-commerce 
exports, district-level export promotion, capacity building and trade promotion. The 
Mission is designed to support exporters across sectors and States, including Tamil 
Nadu, by addressing key bottlenecks and enabling greater integration with global value 
chains. 
The Government is also implementing several measures to improve logistics 
efficiency, reduce transaction costs, simplify export procedures through digital 
initiatives, strengthen port connectivity and multimodal infrastructure, diversify export 
markets through Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and trade promotion activities, and 
facilitate exports from major industrial clusters, thereby contributing to sustained export 
growth from Tamil Nadu and the country as a whole. 
Government has undertaken several initiatives to diversify export markets in light of 
evolving global geopolitical and economic developments. These include expanding 
network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and Comprehensive Economic 
Partnership/Cooperation Agreements (CEPAs/CECAs); pursuing trade negotiations 
with major economies and regions to secure preferential market access for exporters.  
(List of India’s recent Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) is placed at Annexure I, and list 
of Free Trade Agreements/CECA/CEPA/ETCA under negotiation is placed at 
Annexure II)  
Further, as per the National Logistics Policy, one of the primary objectives is to reduce 
logistics costs in India.  The government has also launched initiatives such as the PM 
Gati Shakti National Master Plan, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Bharatmala Pariyojana, 
Sagarmala Programme, Integrated Check Posts, and the Unified Logistics Interface 
Platform (ULIP) for comprehensive development of the logistics sector. 
The Trade Connect Portal, launched in September 2024, is the Government of India’s 
integrated digital platform for trade promotion and facilitation. It serves as a single-
window interface for exporters, importers, industry stakeholders, and government 
institutions to access trade-related information, services, and support. The platform 
brings together tariffs, FTAs, product and market intelligence, Certificates of Origin, 
buyer discovery, trade events, e-commerce guidance, export certifications, and expert 
advisory services in one place, enabling a more seamless and efficient export 
ecosystem.  
A new Central Sector Scheme, Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA) with total 
financial outlay of ₹ 33,660 crore has been rolled out by the Government of India  The 
Scheme aims to develop 100 investment-ready, world-class plug-and-play industrial 
parks that enable investors to establish manufacturing facilities with ease, thereby 
strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity and supporting integration with

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1407 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
 
  DIGITAL CONNECTIVITY INITIATIVES  
  
1407. SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B:  
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  whether digital connectivity initiatives have been extended to Panchayats, if so, the 
details thereof and effectiveness in bridging rural-urban digital divide; 
  
(b)  whether coordination between Central and State agencies is adequate for connectivity 
projects, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for delays and inefficiencies in 
implementation; 
  
(c)  whether public transport services have been expanded to link rural Panchayats with 
cities, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for limited accessibility for rural 
populations; 
  
(d)  whether private sector participation has been encouraged in rural connectivity projects, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons for underutilization of private investment 
opportunities; and 
  
(e)  whether the Government has identified connectivity-deficient Panchayats, if so, the 
details thereof and the targeted measures proposed to address regional disparities in 
infrastructure development? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) & (b)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has undertaken various digital governance 
initiatives under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) to strengthen the functioning of 
Panchayati Raj Institutions. The Ministry has developed digital applications such as 
eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline and mActionSoft to facilitate planning, financial management, 
accounting, audit, monitoring of works and service delivery by Panchayats. The Ministry also 
continuously upgrades these applications and integrates them with other Government digital 
platforms to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability in Panchayat governance. 
The Ministry works in coordination with the respective State Governments and other 
Ministries/Departments, wherever required, for the implementation and integration of digital 
governance initiatives.  

2 
 
In addition, as per the information furnished by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), 
the BharatNet project is being implemented in a phased manner to create a broadband network 
connecting all Gram Panchayats (GPs) across the country. The BharatNet infrastructure is made 
available to Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) for 
extending broadband services to Gram Panchayats, rural areas, Government institutions, schools 
and other users. As of June 2026, out of 2,63,447 Gram Panchayats/ Traditional Local Bodies 
(TLBs) planned to be connected under BharatNet, 2,21,780 Gram Panchayats have been 
connected for the provision of high-speed broadband services. 
Further, the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 
04.08.2023 for upgradation of the existing BharatNet Phase-I and Phase-II network, creation of 
network in the remaining Gram Panchayats, and operation and maintenance of the network for a 
period of ten years.  
(c) to (e)  The development and operation of public transport services, including connectivity 
between rural areas and urban centres, as well as the promotion of private sector participation in 
connectivity infrastructure, are primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments 
and the concerned Ministries/Departments. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not implement 
any scheme specifically for expansion of public transport services or connectivity infrastructure 
linking rural Panchayats with cities. Accordingly, information regarding the expansion of such 
services, private sector participation in such projects, and identification of connectivity-deficient 
Panchayats is not maintained by this Ministry.

NATIONAL TECHNICAL TEXTILES MISSION 
 
1409.   SHRI CHAVDA VINOD LAKHAMSHI:  
            SHRI RAMESH AWASTHI:  
            SHRI KHAGEN MURMU: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details of total number of international and national conferences organized, so far to 
attract investment under the Promotion and Market Development component of the National 
Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM);  
(b) whether the domestic technical textiles industry has recorded a net trade surplus, as per the 
latest Trade Balance data and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether any strategic roadmap has been formulated to scale up the market value of the 
domestic technical textiles market as per the global benchmarks by the year 2030; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a):  The Ministry of Textiles launched National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) in the 
year 2020 with  a view to boost technical textile sector in the country.  Under Component -II 
(Promotion and Market Development) of NTTM, a total of 47 National/International conferences 
have been organized/participated in by the Ministry of Textiles. 
  
(b):  Yes, the domestic Technical Textiles industry has recorded a net trade surplus of Rs. 
3,420.20 crore in F.Y. 25-26. The details thereof are as under:  
Parameters FY 2025-26 (INR in Crore) 
India Export of Technical Textiles  29,217.60 
India's Import of Technical Textiles 25,797.40 
Balance of Trade in Technical Textiles 3,420.20 
       Source: DGCIS, Ministry of Commerce 
  

(c) & (d):  The National Technical Textiles Mission is focused on promoting indigenous 
development and commercialisation of value -added Technical Textiles products, including 
critical segments such as agro -textiles, geo -textiles, medical textiles, industrial textiles,  
protective textiles, and sportech, among others. The Mission also undertakes creation of 
awareness among stakeholders, user Ministries/Departments, and the general public regarding 
the applications and benefits of Technical Textiles through workshops, con ferences, exhibitions, 
and skill development programmes. Further, use of Technical Textiles items has also been 
recommended for mandatory adoption in specified applications by various end -user 
Ministries/Departments/State Governments, wherever feasible, to  create sustained domestic 
demand. 
 
  The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles, which covers Technical 
Textiles as one of its focus segments, has been introduced to enable the textile sector to achieve 
scale and competitiveness at a global  level. The Scheme is designed to address India's structural 
gaps in the Man -Made Fibre (MMF) and Technical Textiles value chain, and to encourage 
investment in high value -added segments, thereby enhancing production capacity, technology 
adoption, and expo rt competitiveness of the sector.  
 
  These measures, taken together, are expected to give a significant impetus to the growth of 
the domestic Technical Textiles industry and to enhance its share in global trade.

FUNDS TO HIMACHAL PRADESH UNDER AIF 
1410. MS KANGNA RANAUT: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी    
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of post-harvest losses in horticulture regions due to 
inadequate cold storage, processing and supply chain infrastructure and if so, the reasons 
therefor, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the details of number, status of projects and funds disbursed under the Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund (AIF) in Himachal Pradesh, district-wise; 
(c) the details of infrastructure created under the scheme, including CA storage, cold 
chains, pack houses and grading units, State/UT-wise; 
(d) whether challenges faced by farmers, particularly small and marginal farmers in hilly 
areas in accessing institutional credit under the scheme have been assessed, if so, the 
measures taken thereon; 
(e) whether any special provisions are proposed for Himalayan States; and 
(f) the details of awareness and outreach measures for small and marginal horticulture 
farmers? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी    (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) : The Government is implementing various schemes to address infrastructure gaps and 
to strengthen post-harvest infrastructure across the country. Agriculture Infrastructure 
Fund (AIF) facilitates medium- to long-term debt financing for creation of post-harvest 
management infrastructure and viable farming assets, including warehouses, cold stores, 
pack houses, sorting and grading units, assaying units, primary processing centres, 
ripening chambers, logistics facilities etc. The Scheme provides 3% interest subvention 
and credit guarantee support on loans up to ₹2 crore for eligible borrowers, subject to a 
maximum lending rate of 9% per annum. The Mission for Integrated Development of 
Horticulture (MIDH) promotes, holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, 
vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic & medicinal 
plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa. The Scheme envisages support for creation of post-
harvest management (PHM) and marketing for better price realization of produce. The 
Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) scheme supports creation and upgradation of 
scientific storage capacity and other agricultural marketing infrastructure through loan cum 
back-ended capital subsidy. These interventions strengthen the post-harvest value chain 
and help reduce post-harvest losses including in horticulture-producing regions.  

 
 
(b) : Under AIF, since July 2020 till date, total 1,184 projects with a loan amount of Rs. 
598.90 crore have been sanctioned in Himachal Pradesh. The district-wise details of 
projects sanctioned, loan amount, loan disbursed is at Annexure-I.  
(c) : The State wise details of the infrastructure created under AIF including storage, cold 
chains, pack houses and grading units, is placed at Annexure-II. 
(d) & (e) : AIF is implemented uniformly across the country, including hilly and Himalayan 
States, to facilitate access to institutional credit for farmers, including small and marginal 
farmers, through eligible entities such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Primary 
Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Marketing Cooperatives 
Societies. An online single-window of AIF Portal has been developed for application 
submission, approval and monitoring of projects under AIF. 
 (f) : Under the AIF scheme, outreach activities are undertaken through State 
Governments, Central Programme Management Unit (CPMU), State Programme 
Management Units (SPMUs), Banks, NABARD, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), 
Cooperatives, Self Help Groups (SHGs) etc. to inform and educate farmers about the 
benefits and provisions of the scheme by way of workshops, webinars, Krishi Melas, 
exhibitions, FPO interactions etc. As part of the outreach, handholding support for project 
identification, preparation of Detailed Project Report, bank linkage and portal-based 
application is also provided to prospective beneficiaries.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1412 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
 
NATIONAL ELECTRIC VEHICLES POLICY 
 
†1412. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that several States have implemented different policies and 
incentives to promote Electric Vehicles (EVs);  
 
(b) whether the Government is proposing to formulate a comprehensive National Electric 
Vehicle Policy or National Framework to ensure uniformity in standards, charging infrastructure, 
battery recycling, safety standards, and incentives across the country;  
 
(c) whether the Government has sought consultation with State Governments, industry, and 
research institutions in this regard;  
 
(d) whether there is a provision to promote indigenous manufacturing of EVs, batteries, and other 
key components, and private investment under the proposed policy/framework; and  
 
(e) the details of steps being taken by the Government for the deve lopment of a balanced and 
coordinated EV eco-system across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): Yes.  
 
(b): No National Electric Vehicle Policy or National Framework is under consideration in the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries. 
 
(c) & (d): Question does not arise in view of part (b). 
 
(e): The Schemes being implemented by the Government for the development of a  balanced and 
coordinated EV eco-system across the country are as under: 
 
(i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India 
(FAME India) Scheme Phase -II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of 
five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. T he 
scheme provided demand incentive for e -2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting 
up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 
16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e -2Ws, e-3Ws, and e -4Ws. In ad dition, 5,197 electric 
buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of 
₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the 
country. 
 
 
 
 
 

-2- 
 
(ii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component 
Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilitie s 
for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay 
of ₹25,938 crore.  
 
(iii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced  
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.202 1 notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 
(iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovativ e Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) 
Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This 
scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including 
e-2W, e -3W, e -Trucks, e -buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging 
stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An 
allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses 
out of which 13,800 e -buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus 
population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 
200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has 
been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Station on pan India basis.   
 
(v) PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified 
on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 
38,000 electric bu ses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e -bus 
operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). 
 
(vi) Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India 
(SPMEPCI) was notified on 15th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of electric cars in 
India. This scheme requires applicants to invest a minimum of ₹4,150 crore and to achieve a 
minimum DVA of 25% at the end of the third year and DVA of 50% at the end of the fifth year. 
 
 Further, follow ing initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to 
increase the use of electric vehicles in the country:– 
 
i.  GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been 
reduced to 5%. 
 
ii.  Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery -operated 
vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. 
 
iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help 
reduce the initial cost of EVs.

the delay in the disbursement of subsidies to farmers under the drip irrigation scheme 
in the Parbhani, Washim-Yavatmal Parliamentary Constituencies; and 
(e) if so, the time-frame fixed for its implementation, and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
  

(a):  Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, 
Ministry of Jal Shakti is implementing Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme 
(PMKSY-AIBP) and Har khet Ko Pani Components of PMKSY which focuses on major, 
medium and minor irrigation projects. Three major and medium irrigation projects are 
benefiting the Parbhani and Yavatmal Parliamentary Constituencies under the 
Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme and Central Assistance amounting to Rs. 
601.92 crore has been released for these projects with an irrigation potential of 37.62 
thousand hectares created, so far. Further, 14 minor irrigation projects in Yavatmal 
district and 18 minor irrigation projects in Washim district have been included under 
the Special Package for Maharashtra. Central Assistance of Rs. 22.52 crore and Rs. 
39.60 crore has been released with creation of an irrigation potential of 5,403 hectares 
and 4,192 hectares in Yavatmal and Washim districts respectively. 
 
(b):  The Government is implementing yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index-based Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) to provide financial support to farmers against crop 
losses due to natural calamities and adverse weather events. PMFBY is voluntary for 
States/UTs and farmers. To make claim settlement simple, transparent and time-
bound, the Government has developed the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) for 
online enrolment, subsidy management and direct transfer of claims into farmers' bank 
accounts. The Digiclaim Module integrated with PFMS has been operationalised from 
Kharif 2022 for transparent claim processing. Further, from Kharif 2024, a penalty of 
12% is auto-calculated on delayed payment by Insurance Companies. From Kharif 
2025, a 12% penalty is also levied on delayed release of State share of subsidy in 
addition to opening of ESCROW account for advance deposit of premium share by 
States has been made mandatory. The Government has also leveraged technology 
through CCE-Agri App, YES-TECH, integration of land records with NCIP and 
mandatory use of Crop Loss Assessment App (CLAP) for faster and transparent claim 
settlement. 
  

(c):  Government is promoting organic farming in all States/UTs including 
Maharashtra through Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Paramparagat Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PKVY) since 2015-16. The scheme provides end-to-end support covering 
production, processing, certification and marketing, with preference to small and 
marginal farmers through formation of organic clusters including training on all aspects 
of organic farming. Under PKVY, financial assistance of Rs.31,500 per hectare for 
three years, including Direct Benefit Transfer of Rs.15,000 per hectare for on-farm/off-
farm organic inputs are provided to beneficiary farmers. In Maharashtra, since 
inception of the scheme, Central assistance of Rs.165.56 crore has been released 
and 69,852 hectare has been covered benefitting 91,259 farmers. District wise details 
are not maintained centrally.   
 
(d) & (e): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India 
is implementing Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme 
in the Country including Maharashtra. The scheme is implemented by the States/UTs 
as per their Annual Acton Plan (AAP). Under PDMC Scheme, financial assistance is 
provided to farmers for installation of micro irrigation systems @ 55% and 45% of the 
unit cost to small & marginal farmers and other farmers respectively. In addition to 
above, State Government of Maharashtra is providing top-up subsidy with effective 
assistance @ 80% and 75% of the unit cost to small & marginal farmers and other 
farmers respectively. During Current Financial Year, Central Assistance of Rs.249.76 
cr is allocated to State under PDMC-PMRKVY against which 1st Mother Sanction has 
been issued for Rs. 124.88 crore. During the last three years, an area of 8336.75 ha 
in Parbhani District, 10336.04 ha area in Washim District and 15438.82 ha in of area 
in Yavatmal District has been covered under micro irrigation through PDMC.

MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
UPDATION OF DATA ON E-MARG PORTAL 
 
1415. Shri Lalji Verma: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken cognizance that permanent 
roads are being laid directly on soil without adequate bitumen 
in the rural areas of Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether it is true that  maintenance data is updated on the e-
Marg portal, rural youth are facing serious accidents while 
commuting to markets and educational institutions due to 
physical potholes on these roads, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government will revise the standards to increase 
the thickness and load bearing capacity of rural roads in view of 
the pressure from cargo-carrying vehicles, if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d)  whether Social Audit reports from local Gram Sabhas will be 
made mandatory before road construction in rural Uttar Pradesh 
to curb corruption? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
  
(a):   Roads under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) 
are constructed as per the Standard Bidding Document (SBD), the 
Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) Specifications for Rural Roads, 
and the standards prescribed by the Indian Road Congress (IRC). 
PMGSY roads are built with properly designed pavement layers, 
including sub-grade, Granular Sub-Base (GSB), base course, and 
bituminous surfacing using the prescribed quality and quantity of 
materials. 

Page 2 of 3 
 
To ensure construction quality, a three-tier Quality Management 
System is followed: 
I. First Tier: Quality checks by the contractor and the Programme 
Implementation Unit (PIU);  
II. Second Tier: Inspections by State Quality Monitors (SQMs) 
appointed by the State Rural Roads Development Agency 
(SRRDA); and  
III. Third Tier: Independent inspections by National Quality 
Monitors (NQMs) empanelled by the National Rural 
Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA). 
(b):    The electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads (e-MARG) portal is 
an enterprise GIS-based solution for monitoring routine maintenance 
of PMGSY roads during their 5-year Defect Liability Period (DLP) and 
post-DLP. Maintenance activities and contractor payments are 
performance-linked and verified via geo-tagged images. While 
localized potholes or surface damages may occur due to severe 
weather or heavy traffic loads, immediate repairs are mandated 
under contract conditions. Citizen feedback and complaints 
regarding potholes/damaged roads are received through the "Meri 
Sadak" mobile application, enabling field officers to take time-bound 
corrective action. 
  
(c):   PMGSY roads are designed in accordance with the relevant IRC 
standards, keeping in view the expected traffic, soil conditions and 
local requirements. Under PMGSY-III, the focus has been shifted 
towards consolidating Through Routes (TRs) and Major Rural Links 
(MRLs) connecting inter-alia to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), 
Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals. Higher design criteria, 
including increased pavement thickness, improvements in sub-
grades strengths, and improved carriageway width upto 5.5m have 
been allowed to handle higher traffic volume on these routes.  Design 
specifications are continuously updated by Indian Road Congress 
(IRC) and the same is followed by the Ministry. However, if the 
States/UTs propose specifications above the permitted IRC norms, 
the same is permissible with the additional cost being borne by the 
concerned States/UTs.  
  
(d):    Under PMGSY guidelines, transparency and community 
participation are integral. Citizen Information Boards are installed at 
construction sites detailing project cost, technical specifications, 
and maintenance period details. Community engagement and public 
monitoring are facilitated through the Meri Sadak App and public 
accessibility of road status via the OMMAS/PMGSY Portal. QR codes 

Page 3 of 3 
 
have also been made mandatory on all PMGSY roads to enable the 
citizen to have all the information about the specific road.  While 
project execution and technical implementation are the primary 
responsibility of the concerned State Quality Control Cell (SQCC) and 
Program Implementation Units (PIUs), quality assurance is ensured 
through a three-tier monitoring system comprising State Quality 
Monitors (SQMs) and independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs). 
Public disclosures and social accountability mechanisms are 
encouraged in coordination with State Governments.  
  
As part of PMGSY guidelines, all States are required to include a 
simple, non-formal “transect walk” to be organized by the Assistant 
Engineer along with Panchayat Pradhan, local patwari and Junior 
Engineer at the time of preparation of DPRs. At the end of the 
Transect Walk, a Gram Sabha Meeting shall be held and alignment 
shall be finalised after recording the issues that arose during the walk 
and the action taken/proposed to resolve the issues. This shall be 
reduced to in writing as Minutes of the Gram Sabha Meeting signed 
by the Pradhan/Panch, Intermediate/District Panchayat Member, if 
present, Secretary of the Gram Panchayat, other officials and Gram 
Sabha Members present. A copy of these Minutes and photographic 
and video graphic records of the Transect Walk shall be attached to 
the finalised DPR.

provided under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) and other horticulture development schemes 
for interventions such as protected cultivation, micro-irrigation, mulching and other horticulture development 
technologies to promote their adoption by farmers;

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 28th July, 2026 
 
Support to Farmers under MIDH 
 
1418:  SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR: 
           SHRI TANGELLA UDAY SRINIVAS: 
 
Will     the     Minister     of AGRICULTURE     AND     FARMERS     WELFARE     
 कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण मंýी  be pleased to state:                       
(a) whether the Government provides any dedicated institutional, technical or extension support under 
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) to assist farmers in the adoption, installation, 
operation and maintenance of protected cultivation infrastructure and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the operational guidelines of MIDH provide for the engagement of NGOs, private sector entities 
or other technical agencies to provide such support and if so, the eligibility criteria and process for their 
engagement; 
(c) the number and names of such organisations engaged in the States/UTs under MIDH, during each of 
the last five years, State/UT-wise; 
(d) whether any financial assistance or cost-sharing mechanism is available under MIDH for providing 
technical handholding, training or extension support through such agencies; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to strengthen the institutional support framework for protected 
cultivation and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण राºय मंýी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) Government is implementing the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), a 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme for holistic development of the horticulture sector in the country. Under 
MIDH, institutional, technical and extension support is provided to assist farmers in the adoption of 
protected cultivation technologies. Such support is provided through State Horticulture Missions, Technical 
Support Groups (TSGs), Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of Excellence (CoEs), 
ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other 
recognised institutions.  

The National Horticulture Board (NHB) also provides institutional and technical support through 
implementation of programmes such as the Clean Plant Programme, Horticulture Cluster Development 
Programme. Centres of Excellence established under MIDH serve as demonstration and training centres 
and act as sources of elite planting material and vegetable seedlings under protected cultivation. Sixty-
one (61) crop-specific Centres of Excellence have been established under MIDH through Indo-Israel 
Cooperation, Indo-Dutch Cooperation and Research Institutes. In addition, assistance is available for 
demonstrations, capacity building and training of farmers and field functionaries under the Human 
Resource Development (HRD) component of MIDH.  
(b) to (d) The Operational Guidelines of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture 
(MIDH) do not contain any specific provision for engagement of NGOs or private sector entities. 
However, under Mission Management component of MIDH, 2.5% of total annual allocation is provided 
to State Horticulture Missions for managing various activities at State & District level. 
(e) MIDH scheme also provides support for strengthening institutional support framework for protected 
cultivation through Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs), Centres of Excellence (CoEs), 
State Horticulture Missions, National Horticulture Board (NHB), ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural 
Universities and Krishi Vigyan Kendras. Further, financial and technical assistance is provided under 
MIDH for construction of protected cultivation structures like poly house, shade net house, plastic/non-
woven cloth tunnels, walk in tunnels etc. 
Apart from the above, assistance is provided for promotion of protected cultivation at commercial scale 
through National Horticulture Board (NHB) for establishment of integrated commercial horticulture 
production/processing projects including components such as planting materials, plantation, irrigation, 
fertigation, mechanization etc.

Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP)-related programmes. During the year 2025–26, 1,90,576 
trainings were imparted under Theme 5 – Clean and Green Village, which includes effective 
operation of solid and liquid waste management, sanitation and public utilities at the local level. 
Further, the Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended that 50% of the Basic Grant be 
earmarked for 'Sanitation and Solid Waste Management' and/or 'Water Management'. Flexibility 
has been provided to Rural Local Bodies to utilize these funds in accordance with local 
requirements, including operation and maintenance (O&M) of sanitation infrastructure, solid and 
liquid waste management, water management. This financial support enables Gram Panchayats 
to effectively deliver essential public services at the local level. 
Further, under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), the Ministry has developed digital 
applications such as eGramSwaraj and mActionSoft to facilitate planning, implementation and 
monitoring of Gram Panchayat Development Plans and geo-tagging of assets and works, 
including those relating to sanitation and waste management. These applications promote 
transparency, accountability and effective monitoring of Panchayat activities. 
(c)  No such scheme is being implemented by Ministry of Panchayati Raj, however, the 
Ministry continues to strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions through initiatives such as the 
Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) for capacity building and the e-Panchayat 
Mission Mode Project (MMP) for promoting digital governance, planning, transparency and 
efficient service delivery. Employment generation and self-employment programmes for rural 
youth are implemented by the concerned Ministries/Departments through their respective 
schemes, with Panchayati Raj Institutions playing an important role in local planning and 
implementation, wherever applicable.

socio-economic welfare of traditional fishermen and fish farmers in Ramanath apuram district in

Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (2023 -24 to 2026 -27) and Extension of the

 (c): The details  of fisheries infrastructure developed in Ramanathapuram district, including

(d):    The Government organizes various skill development and capacity-building programmes for 
fishermen and fish farmers to enhance their technical skills, disseminate recent innovations and best 
practices in the fisheries sector, and promote sustainable livelihood opportun ities. These training

families. 88 training programs covering about 5599 trainees were conducted in the previous 3 years 
for fishers and fish farmers in Ramanathapuram district. The details are given in Annexure III.

assistance and institutional credit is provided for acquisition of 45 deep-sea tuna fishing vessels. In

as seaweed cultivation and cage culture are being actively promoted to provide alternative

to-eat fish products, boat driving, marine engine repair and maintenance, net crafting, and recycling

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ िष एवं िकसान कÐयाण राºय

(a) whether the Union and State Governments have prepared any special contingency plan in view 
of the possibility of deficient rainfall in all the districts of the State of Uttar Pradesh including 
Ayodhya Division and Bundelkhand regions during the current monsoon season;  
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the number of districts of Uttar Pradesh which have been declared as highly sensitive under 
this plan and the details thereof, district-wise; and 
(d) whether there is any proposal to give special 100% subsidy on seeds of coarse grains like jowar, 
bajra, ragi and oilseeds to bail out the farmers of Bundelkhand from the crisis? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ िष एवं िकसान कÐयाण राºय मंýी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): In view of probability of below normal rainfall during Kharif 2026-27, 262 districts were 
identified and prioritized for monitoring as vulnerable on the basis of the following criteria: - (i) 
Low Surface Irrigation Coverage (<50%): Districts where less than 50% of the agricultural area is 
covered by surface irrigation projects, leaving them majority dependent on monsoon rain. (ii) High 
Probability of Low Rainfall (>30%): Districts that have a greater than 30% probability of receiving 
below-normal rainfall during the monsoon. (iii) Districts having more than 20000 Hectares sown 
area during Kharif season 2024-25.  
For these districts, updated District Agriculture Contingency Plans were prepared in 
consultation with State Government officials. These plans included crop strategies for delayed 
monsoon onset, as well as contingency measures to address mid-season and terminal drought 
conditions. The updated district-level crop contingency plans were shared with the State 
Government.  
Further, the ICAR has developed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for KVKs to 
implement these contingency plans. These SOPs encompass development of need based 
contingency plans, implementation procedures, coordination with agriculture department and 
other line departments, release of real time agro-advisories for the district, capacity development, 
awareness generation and real time feedback. 

(c): The districts of Uttar Pradesh identified as vulnerable are Badaun, Chitrakoot, Deoria, 
Farrukhabad, Jhansi, Kheri, Mahoba, Saharanpur, Sonbhadra. Details of contingency plans for 
these districts have been shared with the State Government. 
(d): The Government has approved the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) 
on 3rd October, 2024 for seven-year period, from 2024-25 to 2030-31 to boost domestic oilseed 
production and to strive toward self-reliance in edible oils. 
The mission aims to enhance the production of primary oilseed crops such as Rapeseed & 
Mustard, Groundnut, Soybean, Sunflower, Sesamum, Niger, Safflower, Linseed & Castor as well 
as increasing collection and extraction efficiency from secondary sources like Cottonseed, Rice 
Bran, Corn oil and Tree Borne Oils. The scheme is being implemented in 30 States/UTs including 
Uttar Pradesh.

CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G 
 
1422. Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total number of houses sanctioned and constructed under 
the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Gramin (PMAY-G) in the Dahod 
Lok Sabha Constituency so far and the time by which the 
beneficiaries who are still deprived of will be provided with 
housing facilities; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to relax the eligibility rules 
of the scheme so that the remaining needy families in tribal-
dominated areas like Dahod can get the benefit of this scheme 
soon, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether beneficiaries names have been  removed from the list 
during the recent survey and verification of the final list in the 
Dahod district, if so, the reasons therefor, block-wise; and 
(d)  whether any proposal is under consideration by the Government 
to simplify the rules of this scheme, keeping in view the local 
geographical, economic and tribal conditions so that no poor 
person remains homeless, and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
  
(a): The State of Gujarat has informed on 21.07.2026 that a total of1 
,17,145 houses have been sanctioned by the State in the area falling 
in Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency, out of which 1,15,384 houses have 
been completed . The sanctioning of houses is an ongoing process 
subject to overall allocation, target allocated to states, eligibility of 
beneficiaries and availability of funds. 
(b): As per Framework for Implementation of PMAY-G, a minimum of 
60% of the target allocated to each State/UT is earmarked for 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Scheduled Caste (SC)/Scheduled Tribes (ST) households subject to 
availability of eligible beneficiaries in the Permanent Wait List (PWL). 
The earmarking defines only the minimum limit that should be 
achieved and if the States/UTs so desire, they may add to the target 
under these categories to ensure saturation. Further, the Ministry 
allocates the targets to the State/UT as a whole and District wise/ 
Block-wise/Gram Panchayat wise targets are fixed by the State. 
No proposal for any relaxation in eligibility rules is under 
consideration in the Ministry. 
(c): Beneficiary names have not been removed from the list of those 
surveyed under Awaas + 2024 household survey in Dahod district of 
Gujarat state. However beneficiaries have been marked eligible and 
ineligible based on scheme guidelines. 
(d): In order to enhance inclusivity and ensure that deserving rural 
households are not excluded, the Government has in August 2024 
already approved significant modification of the earlier exclusion 
criteria used for beneficiary identification under PMAY-G. As part of 
these revisions, the provisions related to possession of mechanised 
two-wheelers, mechanized fishing boats, landline telephones and 
refrigerators—which featured in the earlier 13 exclusion criteria—
have now been removed. Further, the monthly income threshold 
under the exclusion criteria has been enhanced from ₹10,000 to 
₹15,000 in view of changed socio-economic realities. The land-
related exclusion parameters have also been simplified, ensuring 
that families with small or non-productive land holdings are not 
disproportionately excluded.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1423. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF PLI SCHEME 
 
1423.  DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the manner in which the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme is being 
implemented; 
 
(b)  the policy adopted to increase exports from the country; 
 
(c)  the steps taken to promote the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) 
sector; 
 
(d)  the reforms introduced to attract foreign investment; and 
 
(e)  the details of India’s industrial position in the global market? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes for 14 key sectors were 
approved with an outlay of ₹1.91 lakh crore with the objective to enhance India's 
manufacturing capabilities, attract investments, promote exports, generate 
employment and reduce import depe ndence. The respective Administrative 
Ministries/Departments are responsible for implementation of the Schemes, 
while the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) acts 
as the nodal Department for overall coordination and monitoring. 
As on 31.03.2026, under the PLI Schemes, 892 applications have been 
approved across 14 sectors, resulting in actual investment of over ₹2.40 lakh 
crore, production/sales of over ₹22.66 lakh crore, exports of over ₹15.2 lakh 
crore, employment generation of over 14.15 lakh (direct and indirect) out of 
which 8.4 Lakhs is Direct employment and cumulative incentive disbursement 
of ₹35,354 crore. The PLI Schemes have also contributed to strengthening 
domestic manufacturing and reducing import dependence across se ctors by 
promoting domestic production of critical products and components, deepening 
local value addition and integrating Indian manufacturers with global value 
chains. 

The sectoral impact of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes across 
various sectors is as under: 
 In the Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing sector, mobile phone  
production has increased by around 2.4 times since the launch of the 
Scheme. Mobile phone imports have declined by about 77%, and around 
99.2% of mobile phones used in India are now manufactured domestically. 
 The Pharmaceuticals sector has recorded cumulative sales of over ₹3.64  
lakh crore under the Scheme. It has also enabled the domestic 
manufacture of 1,931 pharmaceutical products, including 191 bulk drugs 
manufactured in India for the first time, thereby strengthening domestic 
manufacturing capabilities. 
 In the Bulk Drugs sector, manufacturing capacity of about 55,000 MT has 
been established across 26 critical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients 
(APIs), significantly enhancing domestic production capacity and reducing 
import dependence  for products such as Paracetamol, Levofloxacin and 
Norfloxacin. 
 The PLI Scheme for Manufacturing of Medical Devices has facilitated 
domestic manufacturing of advanced medical equipment suc h as CT 
Scanners, MRI Systems, Cath Labs and Ultrasonography equipment. 22 
applicants have commenced operations and 55 unique medical devices 
have been commissioned. 
 In the Telecom & Networking Products sector, the Scheme has supported 
the development of indigenous 4G technology and domestic manufacturing 
capability for 5G telecom equipment, strengthening India's telecom 
manufacturing ecosystem. 
 The PLI Scheme for White Goods has contributed to a significant 
expansion in domestic manufacturing. Compressor manufacturing capacity 
has increased from 1 million units in 2021 to 10 million units in 2025 -26, 
while localisation of key components such as PCBAs and Cross Flow Fans 
has improved substantially, leading to domestic manufacturing of several 
critical air-conditioner components. 
 
(b): The Government is consistently working to boost exports and expand the 
country’s global footprint, combining traditional strengths with emerging  
technology-driven sectors. Central to this ambition is the creation of a 
supportive ecosystem wherein, exporters, particularly MSMEs, can compete 
confidently in international markets. This eﬀort is reinforced by a dynamic policy 
framework, strong financial incentives, a growing digital infrastructure, 
improved trade facilitation, and a determined push to secure deeper market 
access through next-generation trade agreements. 
The RoDTEP scheme plays a central role by neutralizing embedded taxes on 
exports and enabling Indian goods to remain competitive worldwide. The 
recently launched Export Promotion Mission (EPM) further reinforces this eﬀort 
through two targeted pillars: expanding access to aﬀordable trade finance and 
upgrading quality, logistics, branding, and market -readiness across the export 
value chain. The Government has approved the EPM with a budgetary outlay 
of Rs. 25,060 crores (FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31). It operates through Niryat 
Protsahan (focusing on trade finance and credit enhancement) and Niryat 

Disha (focusing on export logistics, warehousing, and market access), 
specifically targeting MSME competitiveness. 
Proactive trade diplomacy complements policy measures and expanding digital 
infrastructure, reinforcing the country’s eﬀorts to strengthen global market 
access and enhance export competitiveness. With 19 FTAs and a renewed 
push since 2021 wherein India has concluded or advanced eight major 
agreements with key partner s. The India -EU FTA, a landmark pact oﬀering 
access to almost the entire EU tariﬀ universe, marks a significant step in 
integrating India more deeply into global value chains. The India -EFTA Trade 
and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) is India’s first FTA to include a 
dedicated commitment aiming to increase FDI from their investors. Trade 
agreements with New Zealand, Oman and UK will broaden market access, 
enhance services mobility, secure long -term investments, and create 
predictable regulatory environ ments for businesses. Meanwhile, ongoing 
negotiations with Israel, Canada, GCC nations, Chile, and Peru indicate India’s 
determination to expand high-value trade corridors across regions. 
India’s export strategy reflects a decisive whole -of-government appr oach, 
moving beyond transactional support to building a resilient, competitive, and 
future-ready ecosystem. By combining targeted financial incentives, 
technology-enabled trade facilitation, institutional reforms, and proactive 
market-access initiatives, t he focus is on embedding digital governance, 
expanding global reach, and strengthening exporter capabilities across sectors 
and regions. This integrated approach positions India not just as a participant, 
but as a trusted, technology-driven partner in global trade. 
(c): The Government has taken a number of initiatives for promotion of MSME 
sector in the country. The recent initiatives for promotion of MSMEs are given 
below: 
 New revised criteria for classification of MSMEs, based on Investment and 
Turnover, to widen the ambit of the MSME sector. 
 “Udyam Registration” for registration of MSMEs, which is a completely 
online, free-of-cost and self-declaration-based portal, thus, promoting Ease 
of Doing Business. 
 Udyam Assist Platform, for bringing Informal Micro Enterprises in the formal 
ambit which helped the registered IMEs to avail the benefits of Priority 
Sector Lending. 
 Inclusion of Retail and Wholesale traders as MSMEs w.e.f. 02.07.2021. 
 Non-tax benefits extended for 3 years in case of an upward change in 
status of MSMEs. 
 Ministry of MSME has launched Samadhaan Portal for filing of grievances 
and monitoring of outstanding dues to the MSEs from the buyers of goods 
and services. 
 Launching of an online Portal “CHAMPIONS” in June, 2020 to cover many 
aspects of e-governance including redressing grievances and handholding 
of MSMEs 
 To support the MSME Sector, the Ministry of MSME implements various 

schemes and programmes for facilitati ng access to credit, marketing, 
skilling, technology upgradation, infrastructure, etc.,  which inter -alia 
includes Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), 
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises, Micro and 
Small Enterprises-Cluster Development Program (MSE-CDP), Public 
Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012, Raising and Accelerating 
MSME Performance (RAMP), Self  Reliant India(SRI) Fund, PM-
Vishwakarma Scheme, Tool Rooms & Technology Centres (TCs) etc. 
 
(d): In recent years, India has been an attractive destination for FDI. India has 
embarked on a series of reforms aimed at liberalising its Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI) policies, with the goal of stimulating economic growth and 
encouraging foreign capital in flows. To promote Foreign Direct Investment 
(FDI), the Government has put in place an investor friendly policy, wherein most 
sectors, except certain strategically important sectors, are open for 100% FDI 
under the automatic route. More than 90% of the FDI inflow is received under 
the automatic route. National Single Window System (NSWS) has also been 
launched as the online single point interface of the Government of India for 
investors to start any industry in India and take requisite permissions. 
Further, to ensure that India remains an attractive and investor friendly 
destination, the Government reviews FDI policy on an ongoing basis and makes 
changes from time to time after having intensive consultations with 
stakeholders including apex industry chambers,  Associations, representatives 
of industries/groups and other organizations taking into consideration their 
views/comments. 
FDI policy provisions have been progressively liberalised and simplified across 
various sectors such as Pension, Other Financial Ser vices, Asset 
reconstruction Companies, Broadcasting, Pharmaceuticals, Single Brand 
Retail Trading, Construction & Development, Power Exchanges, e -commerce 
activities, Coal Mining, Contract Manufacturing,  Digital Media, Civil Aviation 
etc. In the recent past, reforms in the FDI Policy have been undertaken in 
sectors such as Defence, Insurance, Petroleum & Natural Gas, Telecom and 
Space. 
The reforms introduced to attract foreign investment since 2019 are placed 
at Annexure. 
(e): India has emerged as one of the world's fastest-growing industrial economies. 
India has steadily positioned itself as a preferred destination for global 
investors. Over the past decade, consistent reforms, simpler regulations, and a 
stable policy environment have attracted si gnificant investments in 
manufacturing. Initiatives to enhance ease of doing business, coupled with 
targeted sectoral incentives, have reinforced India’s competitiveness as a 
global manufacturing hub. 
Total FDI inflows into India over the last eleven years (2014–25) stood at 
USD 748.78 billion, up 143% compared to USD 308.38 billion received during 

2003–14. India clocked USD 94.53 billion in gross FDI inflows in FY 2025 –26, 
up by 17% year -on-year growth. Manufacturing FDI accelerated 18% to USD 
19.04 billion in FY 2024-25 (from USD 16.12 billion in FY 2023–24). 
India’s electronics manufacturing sector has seen a sixfold rise in production 
and an eightfold surge in exports over the past 11 years. 
India’s pharmaceutical industry is a global powerhouse ranking 3rd in the world 
by volume and 14th in terms of value of production supplying over 50% of global 
vaccine demand and nearly 40% of generics to the US. 
As per economic survey 2024 -25, India’s textile & apparel industry is among 
the largest industry globally, contributing around 2.3% to GDP, 13% to industrial 
production, and 12% to total exports.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28TH JULY, 2026 
 
MEASURE TO MITIGATE RISE IN AGRICULTURAL INPUT COSTS AND DEBT 
 
1425. SHRI VIJAY KUMAR HANSDAK: 
    
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the steep rise in agricultural input costs, 
including fertilizers, seeds, diesel and equipments over the last three years and its impact 
on the net income of small and marginal farmers;  
(b) the comprehensive details of the average debt per agricultural household across 
various States during this period and whether this economic stress is pushing farmers 
into a persistent debt trap; and  
(c) the details of specific institutional measures, subsidy restructuring and credit-relief 
schemes the Government plans to implement to mitigate these rising costs and alleviate 
the agrarian debt crisis? 
 
ANSWER  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a):  Agriculture is a state subject. Union and State Governments take appropriate 
measures from time to time to control the price rise of agricultural inputs. Ministry of 
Agriculture & farmers Welfare supports the States through appropriate policy measures, 
budgetary support and implementation of various schemes/programmes to enhance the 
welfare of farmers and making agriculture remunerative.  
 
The Government has implemented various schemes/ programmes cover the entire 
spectrum of agriculture including credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops 
including horticulture, seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer 
collectives, irrigation, extension, procurement of crops, digital agriculture etc. Additionally, 
Government provides subsidy to ensure the availability of fertilizers to farmers at 
reasonable prices despite volatility in international fertilizer markets. Also the Government 
of India is implementing the integrated Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan 
(PM-AASHA) with the objective of ensuring remunerative prices to farmers and making 
essential commodities available to consumers at affordable prices. The scheme 
components are Price Support Scheme (PSS) and Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF), along 
with Price Deficit Payment Scheme (PDPS) and Market Intervention Scheme (MIS). All 
these interventions are aimed at improving farmers’ incomes including marginal and small 

farmers, increase agricultural productivity, reduce the cost of cultivation, promote crop 
diversification, ensure remunerative returns and making agriculture more sustainable.   
 
The average monthly income of agricultural households in the country is periodically 
estimated through the “Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of Agricultural Households”, 
conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation (MoSPI). As per the latest NSS 77th round of the Survey (January, 2019 – 
December, 2019) in the rural areas of the country, the average monthly income per 
agricultural household from various sources is estimated at Rs. 10, 218/- per month. 
According to the SAS findings, the average monthly income per agricultural household has 
increased from Rs. 6,426 in the agricultural year 2012-13 to Rs. 10,218 in 2018-19. 
 
(b) & (c): As per  Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of Agricultural Households 
conducted by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) during NSS 
77th round (January, 2019 – December, 2019) in the rural areas of the country, the 
estimated average amount of outstanding loan per agricultural household across the 
country is Rs. 74,121. State-wise details of average outstanding loans of agricultural 
households are given in Annexure. 
 
To improve credit access over the long term, the government is implementing a 
100% centrally funded Central Sector Scheme known as the Modified lnterest Subvention 
Scheme (MISS) across various States and UTs in pan India. This scheme aims to provide 
concessional interest rates on short-term agricultural loans obtained by farmers through 
Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) for their working capital requirements. Due to KCC-MISS 
scheme, access to easy and affordable credit has increased significantly to farmers to meet 
their operational needs. Under this scheme, farmers receive KCC loans at a subsidized 
interest rate of 7%. To facilitate this, an up front interest subvention (IS) of 1.5% is provided 
to financial institutions. Additionally, farmers who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% 
Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI), effectively reducing the interest rate to 4% per annum. 
From 2014-15 onwards, the overall flow of institutional agricultural credit has increased 
from ₹8.5 lakh crore to over ₹28 lakh crore during 2025-26 (Prov.) while, the annual 
institutional credit flow to Small and Marginal Farmers has increased from ₹3.47 lakh crore 
to ₹14.77 lakh crore during 2024-25. 
 
Further, to provide assured income support and reduce financial stress among 
small and marginal farmers, the Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) Scheme, a 100% Central Sector Scheme. Under the 
scheme, eligible farmer families receive income support of ₹6,000 per year in three equal 
instalments through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The scheme provides timely liquidity 
for agricultural and household needs, helps reduce dependence on informal credit, and 
complements institutional credit initiatives such as the Kisan Credit Card (KCC). Under 
PM-KISAN scheme, the Government has disbursed over Rs 4.47 lakh Cr. through 23 
installments since inception. Additionally, Government had increased MSPs for all 
mandated Kharif, Rabi and other Commercial crops with a minimum return of 50 percent 
over cost of production from 2018-19 onwards.

MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA

Strengthening Agriculture Cooperatives 
 
1426. Shri Jai Prakash: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the financial viability governance standards and 
business performance of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) across the country, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of PACS that have been computerized, diversified into new economic activities 
and linked with digital banking and e -governance platforms throughout the States and Union 
Territories; and 
(c) the steps taken to enable PACS to provide integrated agricultural services including storage, 
processing, marketing and input supply to farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Yes, Sir. In the backdrop of problems faced by Primary Agricultural Credit Societies 
(PACS) across the country like need for transparency, augmenting income streams to 
strengthen their financial strength, improving governance standards, Government has taken a 
number of measures . To improve governance, transparency and operational efficiency of 
PACS, Model Bye-laws for PACS have been prepared in consultation with all stakeholders 
and circulated to all States/UTs. The Model Bye -laws enable PACS to undertake more than 
25 business activities, improve governance through greater transparency and accountability, 
and make membership more inclusive with adequate representation of women and Scheduled 
Castes/Scheduled Tribes. As per information available with the Ministry, 32 States/UTs have 
adopted the Model Bye-laws or have aligned their existing bye-laws with the Model Bye-
laws. 
Further, the Ministry is implementing several initiatives to improve the financial sustainability 
and business performance of PACS, including: 

Page 2 of 4 
 
i. Computerisation of functional PACS through a common ERP -based national 
software;  
ii. Diversification of PACS into various economic activities;  
iii. Establishment of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and Fisheries Cooperative 
Societies in uncovered Panchayats;  
iv. Convergence of various Central Government schemes for creation of agricultural 
infrastructure at PACS level under the world's largest grain storage initiative in 
the cooperative sector; and  
v. Integration of PACS with digital and e-Governance platforms for efficient service 
delivery. 
(b)  Government of India is implementing this Project of Computerization of functional 
PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has now been increased upto 2925.39 
Crore which entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP (Enterprise Reso urce 
Planning) based common national software, linking them with NABARD through State 
Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). The State wise 
progress made under the project is at Annexure-‘A’. 
The status of diversified activities being carried out by PACS enabled by Model Bye-Laws are 
as follows (as on 15.07.2026):  As on date, out of 64,159 registered PACS, 55,514 are 
functioning as Common Service Centres (CSCs) ; u nder the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya 
Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK) scheme, 4,275 applications have been received from PACS, of 
which 4,255 have received initial approvals, 900 have obtained drug licences, 846 have been 
allotted store codes and 645 centres have become operational;  out of 48,461 PACS functioning 
as fertilizer retailers, 38,974 have been upgraded as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras 
(PMKSKs); 1,480 PACS across 10 States have been selected as Water Committees, of which 
118 have commenced loan recovery work ; a s per information provided by Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs), 394 PACS from 28 States/UTs have applied online for retail petrol/diesel 
outlets and 13 outlets have been commissioned. Further, 115 PACS holding wholesale 
consumer petrol pump licenses in 5 States have agreed to convert their outlets into retail outlets, 
out of which 62 retail outlets have been commissioned. 
The Ministry has also initiated steps to integrate the PACS ERP system with various State s’ 
digital and e -Governance platforms to streamline agricultural credit and service delivery.  In 
Andhra Pradesh, PACS ERP has been integrated with e -Governance Services, Paddy 
Procurement, LPG, MARKFED, the IGRS Registration & Stamp Portal of the Government of 
Andhra Pradesh, the Public Distribution System (PDS), e -Crop and the CCLA (Chief 
Commissioner of Land Administration) platform ; in Bihar, integration has been undertaken 
with the Aadhaar-enabled Public Distribution System (AePDS) and e-Sahkari; in Chhattisgarh, 
PACS ERP has been integrated with the Ekikrit Kisan Portal, Committee Registration Module, 
Khadya Portal, MARKFED, Bhuiyan Citizen UI and the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer 
Protection Department portal ; i n Gujarat, integration has been carried out with the Gujarat 
Cooperative Portal and Any ROR (Any Record of Rights) Gujarat Portal; in Madhya Pradesh, 
integration has been undertaken with MP Bhulekh and the Samagra Samajik Suraksha Mission; 
in R ajasthan, PACS ERP has been integrated with e -Dharti, Rajasthan State Data Centre 
(RSDC), Single Sign -On (SSO), ePDS, Jan Soochna Portal and RajSahakar Portal ; in Uttar 

Page 3 of 4 
 
Pradesh, integration has been completed with the UP Bhulekh Portal  and in Tamil Nadu, 
integration has been undertaken with the Comprehensive Audit Management System (CAMS). 
 
(c ) Apart from diversified activities being carried out by PACS, there are various other steps 
also taken by Government enabling PACS to provide integrated agricultural services are as 
follows: 
 
The Government on 31.05.2023 approved the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in 
Cooperative Sector. The Plan entails creation of various agri infrastructure at Primary 
Agriculture Credit Society (PACS) level, including warehouses, custom hiring center, 
processing units, Fair Price Shops, etc. through convergence of various existing schemes of the 
Government of India (GoI), such as, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural 
Marketing Infrastructure Scheme (AMI), Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechaniz ation 
(SMAM),  Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme 
(PMFME), etc. Under the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, 1,015 
PACS across the country have been identified for construction of godowns and construction 
work has been completed in 313 PACS creating a total capacity of 1.80 LMT. 
The Ministry of Cooperation has also established National Cooperative Exports 
Limited (NCEL) to provide market linkage to cooperative products and services in the 
international markets. So far, National Co -operative Exports Limited (NCEL) has exported 
14,89,102 metric tonnes of 50 agri -commodities valued at ₹5,866.10 crore to 38 countries. 
Similarly, National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) has been established to provide 
market linkage to organic produce. NCOL markets the organic produce under " Bharat 
Organics" brand and its products are available in more than 1100 retail outlets in New Delhi 
and Bengaluru and on e -commerce and quick commerce platforms.  To provide quality,  
certified and affordable seeds (input services) to farmers, Bharatiya Beej Sahkari Samiti

and through its extensive cooperative network, the 'Bharat Beej' brand has  reached

Glassware and Bangle Industry fi nancial assistance amounting to ₹3,676.27 
lakh has been provided to 622 beneficiaries under the ODOP Margin Money 
Scheme, while 415 beneficiaries have received assistance amounting to 
₹491.66 lakh under the ODOP Marketing Development Assistance (MDA) 
Scheme. Furthermore, under the One District One Product (ODOP) Training 

Scheme, 1,775 beneficiaries have been trained to enhance their skills and 
industrial capacity. Upon successful completion of  the training programme, 
each beneficiary has been provided with an advanced toolkit worth up to 
₹20,000. 
Under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment  
(SASCI), financial assistance of up to ₹200 crore per State/UT with legislatures 
- Delhi, Jammu & Kashmir, and Puducherry is provided through a 50 -year 
interest-free loan for establishment of PM Ekta Malls (Unity Malls) to promote 
the sale of ODOP, GI, and local handicraft products. 
(b) & (c): The Government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that no official district -specific 
information has been received from Firozabad's glassware exporters indicating 
any decline in the shipments and a rise in freight costs since March 2026. 
Further, no overall decline has been observed in the exports of Glassware and 
Handicraft during the current financial year compared to previous financial year. 
(d): The Government constituted an Inter -Ministerial Group (IMG) on 02.03.2026 
under the Department of Commerce which meets regularly and coordinate 
measures, including freight subsidy, export credit, duty relief on critical imports, 
implementation of necessary export regulations, and facilitation of alternate 
trade routes, to minimise disruptions to trade and ensure business continuity 
during the ongoing West Asia conflict. 
For freight and insurance support Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India 
(ECGC) has launched the ‘Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export 
Facilitation (RELIEF) ’ intervention on 19.03.2026 with covering exports to the 
West Asia region or sailing through the region. Freight and insurance costs of 
already-sailed exports of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) are 
reimbursed up to 50 lakhs per MSME in respect of non-ECGC covered claims; 
in addition, 100% cover is provided for ECGC -covered exports which had 
already sailed and 95% cover for upcoming exports utilizing ECGC cover.

(a)  whether it is a fact that the old Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) budget was 
slashed by over 60 per cent to Rs. 30,000 crore in the latest 
Union Budget, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(b)  the details and total pending wage liabilities and material 
component arrears carried over into the current financial year, 
State-wise; and 
(c)  the timeline by which the Ministry guarantees the 100 per cent 
liquidation of these historical arrears using the transitional 
allocation? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): A budgetary provision of Rs. 95,692.31 crore has been made 
for Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission 
(Gramin) VB–G RAM G for the FY 2026-27, which will cover the period 
from 01.07.2026 to 31.03.2027. This is among the highest ever 
budgetary allocation made for any Rural Employment Scheme in the 
history of Country at the Budget Estimate stage. In addition, a 
budgetary provision of ₹30,000 crore was made for   Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS for the first three mponths of FY 2026-27 and subsequently, 
an additional budgetary provision of ₹. 6,000 crore was made 
available, taking total budgetary provision under the scheme to ₹ 
36,000 crore for said period of FY 2026-27. 
  
(b) & (c): In the current financial year 2026–27, pending liabilities of 
the wage component amounting to ₹9,711.98 crore have been 
released which includes all admissible pending liability for wage 
component for FY 2025-26. 

Page 2 of 3 
 
  
  For the material component, the Ministry has issued a financial 
sanction amounting to ₹7,765.68 crore as the first installment to all 
States/UTs for release of material liabilities. Out of this an amount 
of ₹5,440.07 crore have so far been utilized by the States/UTs. 
  
  Release of funds to the States/UTs towards settlement of pending 
liabilities under the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi NREGS is a 
continuous process. Funds are released from time to time based on 
the demand for funds, utilization of funds already sanctioned, and 
receipt of complete proposals from the States/UTs along with the 
requisite documents, in accordance with the prescribed procedure 
and Ministry is committed to settle all admissible pending liabilities 
of States/UTs subject to compliance of extant guidelines.
