GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1468 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28th July, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF AIF 
1468.  SHRI MANISH JAISWAL: 
 SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
 SHRI P C MOHAN: 
 SMT. MAHIMA KUMARI MEWAR: 
 SMT. KAMALJEET SEHRAWAT: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी     be pleased to state : 
(a)  the cumulative capital investment leveraged through the Agriculture 
Infrastructure Fund (AIF) for creation of farm-gate storage  and logistics infrastructure 
across the country, State/UT-wise, including Andhra Pradesh, particularly in Palnadu 
district; 
(b)  whether the Bharat-VISTAAR multilingual Artificial Intelligence tool has been 
deployed in Andhra Pradesh and if so, the details thereof, including its role in reducing 
post-harvest losses and improving advisory services to farmers; 
(c)  the steps taken to address operational challenges in the rollout of technology-
driven crop monitoring systems; and 
(d) the measures being taken to expand such technology-enabled post-harvest 
infrastructure and digital agriculture initiatives, State/UT-wise including Andhra Pradesh 
particularly in Palnadu district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
    
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी     (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR)  
(a): As on 15.07.2026, the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) has leveraged a 
cumulative capital investment of ₹1,61,537.22 crore  for the creation of Post harvest 
Infrastructure and viable farming assets including ₹ 50,332.66 crore for creation of 
farm-gate storage and logistics infrastructure. The State wise details are placed at 
Annexure. In Andhra Pradesh the scheme has leveraged a cumulative capital 
investment of ₹2,394.26 crore for farm gate storage and logistic infrastructure. In 
Palnadu district of Andhra Pradesh, 111 projects with a project cost of  ₹209.90 cr 
crore have been sanctioned under the scheme for farm gate storage and logistics 
infrastructure.  
  

 
 
 (b): Bharat-VISTAAR (Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources) 
is a multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered tool conceived as an integrated and 
unified Digital Public Infrastructure platform to provide farmers with reliable, real-time, 
and location-specific personalized agricultural advisories while ensuring seamless 
access to a comprehensive range of allied agricultural and support services. As a 
national platform, it is accessible to farmers across the country, including Andhra 
Pradesh, for information on Central Government agricultural schemes, benefit status 
tracking, grievance redressal, and services such as weather updates, mandi prices, 
ICAR advisories, and other farmer support services, thereby facilitating informed 
decision-making and better crop management by farmers. The platform is available 
through a web portal, mobile application, AI chatbot and dedicated telephone line. At 
present, Bharat Vistaar Telephone service is available in 2 languages, i.e. Hindi and 
English; however, the chatbot, web portal, and mobile application are available in 10 
languages including Telugu. 
(c) & (d):  DA&FW is leveraging satellite-based monitoring and Artificial Intelligence 
(AI)-based analytical systems for forecasting agricultural risks and supporting timely 
crop management interventions across the country including the state of Andhra 
Pradesh. The Krishi Decision Support System (DSS) that integrates and standardizes 
geospatial and non-geospatial data, including satellite, weather, soil, crop signatures, 
reservoir and ground water data, enables monitoring of drought conditions, adverse 
weather events and flood inundation to provide near real-time risk alerts and support 
crop management interventions to reduce risk of crop loss across States/UTs including 
Andhra Pradesh.  
 The Department has launched the National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS) 
which is an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning-based platform that provides 
real-time pest identification, surveillance and expert advisories to farmers on pest 
management across the States/UTs . Further, the system promotes Integrated Pest 
Management (IPM) by recommending bio-control agents and bio-pesticides as the 
preferred option, while advising pesticides duly approved by the Registration 
Committee only when necessary and at recommended doses to prevent crop losses.  
The Government has also introduced yield-based Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop 
Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) from Kharif 2016 to provide financial support to the 
farmers opting for crop insurance against crop loss/damage arising out of natural 
calamities, adverse weather incidence and to stabilize the income of farmers etc. 
Comprehensive risk insurance is provided under the scheme from pre-sowing to post-
harvest losses. Further, with effect from Kharif 2023, Government has rolled out Yield 
Estimation System based on Technology (YES-TECH) wherein yield estimation is 
done using satellite imagery and remote sensing data.   
  

 
 
         The India Meteorological Department (IMD) provides AI-based monsoon and 
weather advisories across the country including the state of Andhra Pradesh to 
support informed agricultural decision-making . The advisories enable farmers to plan 
agricultural operations based on timely and location-specific weather forecasts. As on 
date, the initiative has reached approximately 5.28 crore farmers.  
Krishi Vigyan Kendras are using Krishi Sarthi a ICT based platform to provide 
crop specific advisories to farmers. More than 2.97 cr farmers are registered on this 
platform  
Various steps have been taken to address the operational challenges in roll out 
of technology driven crop monitoring systems including ensuring ease of access to 
digital platforms by the farmers, through web portal, mobile application, SMS alerts , 
AI chatbots and dedicated telephone lines; making various digital services available in 
multiple regional languages for ease of understanding ; provision of dedicated help 
lines to address the queries of farmers along with an effective grievance redressal 
mechanism. In addition technical support and multi level training is provided to the 
States through Project Management Units at the national and state level .

NATIONAL HANDLOOM DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME 
 
1469.   ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details of upgraded looms distributed, worksheds constructed and lighting units installed 
under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) which are currently functional, 
non-functional or abandoned, State/UT-wise;  
(b) the details of Handloom Producer Companies formed under NHDP, including  currently 
active companies, turnover generated, number of member weavers and non -functional or 
dormant entities, State/UT-wise;  
(c) the number of applications received, sanctioned, rejected and pending under the Weaver 
MUDRA Scheme during 2021 -22, along with total amount sanctioned and disbursed thereof, 
State/UT-wise;  
(d) the details of handloom weavers who applied for Weaver MUDRA loans but were unable to 
avail benefits due to procedural delays, State/UT-wise; and  
(e) the details of artisans and weavers onboarded onto the Government e -Marketplace (GeM), 
Indiahandmade, and other digital commerce platforms, along with actual sales generated, active 
users and average earnings through such platforms, State/UT-wise?  
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a): Under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) need based financial 
support is provided for various interventions like upgraded looms & accessories, construction of 
worksheds, lighting units, product & design development etc. State/UT -wise details of upgraded 
looms & accessories, worksheds constructed, lighting units provided under NHDP across the 
country during last three years are at Annexure-A. 
  
(b): The Government promotes the formation and strengthening of Handloom Producer 
Companies (HPCs) as a  key institutional mechanism for organizing handloom weavers into 

professionally managed, member -owned enterprises. 237 Handloom Producer Companies are 
formed under NHDP during 2020-21 to 2025-26. 
  
(c) & (d): Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme is a c omponent of National 
Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) to provide adequate and timely assistance from the 
Banks/financial institutions to the handloom sector to meet their credit requirement for term loan 
& working capital in a flexible and cost -effective manner across the country. Margin money 
assistance is provided @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of Rs.25,000/ - to individual 
handloom weaver/weaver entrepreneur and @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of 
Rs.20.00 lakh (@ Rs.2.00 lakh for eve ry 100 weaver/worker) to handloom organization. 
However, only handloom organizations are eligible for getting loans at concessional interest rate 
of 6% for a period of 3 years subject to interest subvention capped upto 7% by the GoI. Credit 
guarantee fee on loan to handloom organization only is also provided for a period of 3 years.  
  
For timely disbursal of financial assistances i.e. Margin money, Interest Subsidy and Credit 
Guarantee Fee by participating banks, a centralized online claim disbursement sys tem 
“Handloom Weaver Mudra Portal” has been developed in association with Punjab National 
Bank. Margin money is transferred directly to the loan account of beneficiaries and interest 
subsidy is transferred directly to concerned banks through the Portal.  
  
For availing loan under the scheme, eligible handloom weaver/worker is required to approach 
participating bank concerned with the filled -up application and submit it in the bank with 
necessary documents. It is for the bank concerned to satisfy itself with  the eligibility of the 
applicant for grant of loan to the beneficiary. State -wise number of loan and amount of loan 
sanctioned under Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme under NHDP during 2021-22 to 
2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026) is at Annexure-B. 
  
(e): About 1.50 lakh weavers/handloom entities on -boarded on Government e -Marketplace 
(GeM) for marketing of handloom products to the Government Departments. The Government 
has also developed Indiahandmade as a dedicated e -commerce platform for authentic handlo om 
products, including GI -tagged products, enabling verified weavers and producer groups to sell 
directly to consumers. 5413 weavers onboarded onto Indiahandmade platform during 2023 -24 to 
2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026).

ANSWERED ON 28TH JULY, 2026 
 
DAIRY AND LIVESTOCK FARMERS 
 
1471: SHRI ZIA UR REHMAN: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of inadequate veterinary services, fodder shortages and limited 
market access for dairy and livestock farmers in Western Uttar Pradesh;  
(b) if so,  the details of steps taken by the Government to improve animal healthcare, dairy 
infrastructure and farmer’s income in the region;  
(c) whether similar challenges persist in other parts of the country; and 
(d) if so, the details of national initiatives undertake n to strengthen fisheries, animal husbandry and 
dairying sectors? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d)  Animal Husbandry is a state subject and the arrangement of veterinary services and making 
availability of feed and fodder is the mandate of the State Government. The Government of India has 
issued minimum standards of veterinary infrastructure with provisions for fulfilling the standards in a 
phased manner by 2036. The adoption of these guidelines is mandatory under “Special Assistance to 
States for Capital Investment (SASCI)” guidelines. Veterinary services are being provided to farmers by 
the State of Uttar Pradesh through a network of 2,202 veterinary hospitals, 2,575 Livestock Extension 
Officer (LEO) Centers, 267 D-class dispensaries, and 520 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) operating 
to deliver doorstep services to farmers state -wide, including western Uttar Pradesh. There is a shortage 
of fodder in the state. As per ICAR –Indian Grasslands and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi 
estimates, the requirement of green and dry fodder in Uttar Pradesh is 1499.6 lakh tonnes and 735.1 lakh 
tonnes, respectively, against the estimated availability of 1145.0 lakh tonnes of green fodder and 511.5 
lakh tonnes of dry fodder. The Uttar Pradesh Government is implementing a state scheme for all districts 
of Uttar Pradesh namely "Additional Fodder Development Programme (AFDP)", in which department 
is distributing certified fodder seed minikit to the  farmers at free of cost for promoting quality green 
fodder cultivation. Further the State Government of Uttar Pradesh is implementing fodder policy for 
increasing fodder availability through increasing area coverage for fodder production.  
Government of India has taken various initiatives to strengthen fisheries, animal husbandry and dairying 
sector. In this regard, various schemes are implemented by the Government of India in all the states and 
union territories including in the State of Uttar Pradesh. The details are as under: 

 
The Government of India has approved “Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) ” 
wherein the states are eligible to get the incentives after compliance of mandatory conditions. One among 
the mandatory conditions is to increase fodder production by using fund available under VB-GRAM G.  
 
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India  (DAHD, GOI) provides 
financial assistance under National Livestock Mission for genetic improvement of non-bovine livestock, 
insurance, entrepreneurship development, production of good quality fodder seed and fodder.  DAHD, 
GOI released Rs. 3857.00 lakh to the state of Uttar Pradesh during the last three years. 
 
Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) is implemented by the DAHD, GOI to conserve indigenous breed and 
to enhance productivity of cattle and buffalo. National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and 
Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer Producer Organizations (SCDPO) schemes are implemented 
to support, strengthen, expansion of organized milk procurement network . The schemes also envisage 
assistance in  creating and strengthen ing infrastructure for milk processing and value -added product 
manufacturing infrastructure and assisting the cooperative societies and farmer producer organizations 
engaged in dairy activities. 
Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP), 100% central assistance is provided 
for vaccination of targeted animals against economically important diseases, namely Foot and Mouth 
Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF). 
Further, to deliver veterinary services at farmers doorstep, total 4019 mobile veterinary units have been 
provided to 29 States/UTs . Financial support is provided on sharing basis for operations of the same. 
Also, under ASCAD component of LHDCP, financial support on sharing basis is provided to the states 
for prevention and control of state prioritized livestock diseases. 
DAHD, GOI  is also implementing Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) 
Scheme which provides 3% interest subvention for leveraging investment in the establishment of dairy 
processing and value addition infrastructure, meat processing and value addition infrastructure, animal 
feed plant, breed multiplication farm, veterinary vaccine and drugs production facilities, animal waste 
to wealth management (agri-waste management) and primary wool processing infrastructure.  23 Dairy 
Processing and value addition projects with project cost of Rs. 1403.40 lakh have been established in the 
state of Uttar Pradesh since 2020-21. 
 The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of 
India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total investment 
of Rs.20,990.79 crore with effect from the financial year 2020-21 to till date for development of fisheries 
in all States/Union Territories including Uttar P radesh.  Further, the Fisheries Department under the 
PMMSY has accorded approval to the various fisheries developmental proposals of Government of Uttar 
Pradesh at a total cost of ₹.1294.32 crore with central share of ₹. 412.30 crore. An amount of ₹.336.61 
crore has been released to the state of Uttar Pradesh from 2020-21 to 2026-27.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (e) Government accords high priority to export promotion from all districts of the 
country, including Warangal district, through comprehensive measures, including: 
Export Promotion Mission (EPM): approved by the Union Cabinet on November 12, 
2025 with the objective of strengthening India's export competitiveness and providing 
targeted support to exporters in global markets, and a total outlay of ₹25,060 crore 
for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31. EPM is anchored in a collaborative 
framework involving the Department of Commerce, Ministry of MSME, Ministry of 
Finance, and other key stakeholders, including Financial Institutions, Export Promotion 
Councils, Commodity Boards, industry associations, and State Governments. 
 
It operates through two integrated sub-schemes, Niryat Prothsahan, focused on 
improving access to trade finance through instruments such as interest subvention, 
export factoring, collateral guarantees for export credit, credit guarantee for                   
e-commerce exporters, and credit enhancement support; and Niryat Disha, focused 
on other trade enablers such as export quality and compliance support, international 
branding and packaging, market access initiatives, export logistics & warehousing, 
and trade intelligence. 

2 
 
 
Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative: The Government has taken measures to 
identify export potential and promote exports from the districts under this initiative. It 
includes identifying products and services with export potential in all districts of the 
country, in consultation with all stakeholders, including States/UTs. 
 
In order to facilitate grassroots export growth and resolve structural bottlenecks, an 
institutional framework has been established at two levels: State Export Promotion 
Committees (SEPCs) at the State level, and District Export Promotion Committees 
(DEPCs) at the district level. 
 
The core operational mechanism of this initiative relies on the District Export Action 
Plans (DEAPs), which are prepared and implemented by the DEPCs in collaboration 
with Central, State, and District stakeholders. These plans: 
 Identify key products and services with export potential for each district. 
 Outline necessary interventions and identify support required by local industry 
from the production stage through to the exporting stage. 
 Detail specific supply chain bottlenecks and propose targeted mitigation 
strategies. 
 Undergo thorough deliberation by various stakeholders before being formally 
adopted by the respective DEPC. 
As part of DEH framework - export-potential products and services have been identified 
across 734 districts; SEPCs and DEPCs have been successfully constituted in all        
36 States and Union Territories; and DEAPs have been prepared for 713 districts, out 
of which 249 have been formally deliberated and adopted by their respective DEPCs. 
Under the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative, Warangal Rural and Warangal 
Urban districts have identified Textiles, Warangal Durries, Garments, Mango, Riceand 
Maize as products with export potential. 
 
Further, Ministry of Textiles through Office of the Development Commissioner for 
Handlooms is implementing the 'Handloom Marketing Assistance', a component of 
National Handloom Development Programme across the country including the 
Warangal district of Telangana to develop and promote marketing channels in 
domestic and export markets in a holistic and integrated manner to bring greater 
visibility to the sector and ensure commensurate remuneration to weavers. 
Expos are organized including participation in various crafts melas and Dilli Haat 
programme etc., to provide the marketing platforms to the handloom 
agencies/weavers of the country including weavers of Warangal district of Telangana 
to sell their products directly to the customers. Also, an e-commerce portal 
(https://www.indiahandmade.com/) has been launched to support the handloom 
sector for online marketing of handloom products. 
 
In addition, for export promotion of handlooms, financial assistance are provided for 
participation of handloom exporters/weavers of pan India including Warangal district 
of Telangana State in various International marketing events/fairs i.e. International 
Trade Fair, Buyer Seller Meet, Reverse Buyer Seller Meet, Big Ticket events, Bharat 
Tex, are organized through Handloom Export Promotion Council (HEPC). 
 
 

3 
 
 
 
‘India Handloom’ brand (IHB) has been launched on the occasion of First National 
Handloom day on August 07, 2015 with the objective to promote production of niche 
handloom products with high quality, authentic traditional designs with zero defect 
and zero eﬀect on environment. The Salient Features include: 100% Handloom 
products, made of 100% Natural fibres, assured Fast Colours, Skin Friendly Dyes and 
Socially Compliant. 
 
Further, ‘Handloom Mark’ scheme has already been under implementation across the 
country since 2006, including Warangal district of Telangana which serves as a 
guarantee to the buyers that the handloom products being purchased are genuinely 
hand-woven.

IMPLEMENTATION OF NATIONAL STEEL POLICY 2017 
 
 
 
1474.  SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government provide the status of progress towards achieving the 
target of 300 million tonnes of annual crude steel production capacity by 2030-31 
envisaged under the National Steel Policy, 2017, State/UT-wise; 
 
(b) the details of the installed crude steel production capacity, actual crude steel 
production during the last five years and the gap between the present level and the 
target envisaged under the National Steel Policy, 2017, State/UT-wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the National Steel 
Policy, 2017 and if so, the details of the policy targets that have not been achieved 
within the prescribed timelines during the last five years, along with the reasons 
therefor; and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to revise the National Steel Policy, 2017 in view 
of emerging challenges such as Green Steel, decarbonisation and changing global 
trade dynamics, if so, the details thereof?? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
 
(a)to(d):  Steel is a deregulated sector and the government acts as a facilitator by 
creating a conducive policy environment for the development of the steel sector. 
Decisions regarding setting up of steel plants, downstream industries, investment, 
capacity expansion etc. are based on techno-commercial analysis of the individual 
steel companies. The National Steel Policy, 2017 envisages creation of 300 million 
tonnes (MT) of crude steelmaking capacity and production of 255 MT of crude steel 
by 2030-31. The country's crude steelmaking capacity has increased from 154.06 MT 
in 2021-22 to 220.41 MT in 2025-26. Crude steel production has increased from 
120.29 MT to 170.15 MT in the same period.

O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1476 
  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
PROPOSAL FOR CONSTRUCTION OF ROADS UNDER PMGSY 
 
1476. Shri Bhausaheb Rajaram Wakchaure: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether any proposal has been received under the Pradhan 
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) for the improvement or 
construction of roads in the Sangamner and Akole talukas of 
Ahilyanagar district in the State of Maharashtra; 
(b)   if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government is aware of the pathetic condition of 
these rural roads and the potential risks of accidents caused by 
them, if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  whether important roads connecting to the Shirdi pilgrimage 
site will be included in the special priority list, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(e) whether the necessary budget allocation for these road works 
has been approved, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  the details of timeline set by the Government to commence the 
construction work on these roads? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
  
(a) & (b): The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was 
launched in 2000, as a onetime special dispensation, for providing 
connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations in the country. For 
the state of Maharashtra, a total of 24,782 km road length has been 
sanctioned under new connectivity and upgradation components 
under PMGSY-I, out of which 24,184 km road length has been 
completed till 23rd July, 2026. Under PMGSY-II, a total of 2619 km 
road length has been sanctioned under the scheme and 2586 km has 
been completed as on 23rd July, 2026. Under PMGSY-III, a total of 
6,404 km road length has been sanctioned to the state of 

Page 2 of 3 
 
Maharashtra and 5576 km road length has been completed till 23rd 
July, 2026. 
  
So far, under various verticals of PMGSY, 281 road works of 
1819 km length and 26 bridges were sanctioned to Ahilyanagar 
district (formerly Ahmednagar), out of which 256 road works of 1669 
km road and 19 bridges have already been constructed. Under various 
verticals of PMGSY, in Akole taluk 140 road works of 782 km length 
and 21 bridges were sanctioned, out of which 140 road works of 767 
km road and 20 bridges have already been constructed. Sangamner 
Taluk is located in Ahilyanagar district. 
 
In September 2024, the Government of India launched PMGSY 
IV. The primary objective of PMGSY-IV is to provide all-weather road 
connectivity to about 25,000 unconnected habitations of population 
size (as per Census 2011) 500+ in plains, 250+ in Special Category 
States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Ladakh, Manipur, Meghalaya, 
Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu 
Kashmir and Uttarakhand), Special Category Areas [(Tribal Schedule-
V Areas, Desert Areas, Aspirational Blocks/ Districts and Hilly areas 
as notified by the respective State Government (cross slope more 
than 25% gradient and the elevation is more than 600 meters from 
the Mean Sea Level)] and 100+ in LWE affected Districts including 
Legacy & Thrust Districts identified by MHA from time to time. Under 
PMGSY-IV, habitations identified under VVP-II are being prioritised for 
all-weather road connectivity. 
  
Under Batch-I of PMGSY-IV, for the state of Maharashtra, 
sanction has been issued on 18.05.2026 for 35 roads (95.99 km) 
costing Rs. 122.98 crore benefiting 35 habitations. Further, sanction 
of 62 Long Span Bridges (2923.45 m) costing Rs. 252.21 crore has 
been issued under Batch-I of PMGSY-III on 13.07.2026. The State-
wise, District-wise and Parliamentary Constituency-wise details of 
rural road projects and the stages of construction under various 
verticals of PMGSY may be accessed at the programme website 
https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb on a real-time basis. 
  
(c): As per Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) guidelines, 
maintenance of roads constructed under the programme is the 
responsibility of the State/UT Governments. However, the Ministry on 
its part has taken the following steps to ensure proper maintenance 
of roads constructed under PMGSY: 
(i)  All road works sanctioned under the scheme are covered by 
initial five-year maintenance contracts to be entered into along with 

Page 3 of 3 
 
the construction contract, with the same contractor, as per the 
Standard Bidding Document. 
(ii)  Maintenance funds to service the contract are required to be 
provisioned for by the State Governments and placed at the disposal 
of the State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDAs) in a 
separate maintenance account. On expiry of this 5-year post 
construction maintenance, PMGSY roads are required to be placed 
under Zonal maintenance contracts consisting of 5-year maintenance 
including renewal as per maintenance cycle, from time to time, to be 
funded by the State/UT Governments. 
(iii)  Further in order to ensure that States/UTs provide required 
maintenance funds during the design life of the road being 
constructed under PMGSY-III, a provision has been added in the 
programme guidelines under which the states have to enter into a 
Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Rural 
Development, Government of India before launching of the scheme in 
the concerned State/UT for providing adequate funds for the 
maintenance of roads constructed/upgraded under PMGSY for initial 
five years routine maintenance, and for further five year routine 
maintenance including periodic renewal as per requirement. 
(iv)  Release of maintenance funds is required to be certified by the 
State/UT, as per PMGSY guidelines, while submitting fund release 
proposals to the Central Government.   
(v)  Electronic Maintenance of PMGSY roads (e-MARG), an online 
platform, has been implemented in all the States to monitor 
maintenance of PMGSY works for five years from the date of 
completion (i.e. under Defect Liability Period- DLP). Consequent upon 
the introduction of e-MARG i.e. software module for maintenance 
payments to the contractor during the defect liability period, such 
payments have been made commensurate with the quality of roads 
through a performance-based contract management system.  
(d) to (f):  As per the detailed guidelines for implementation of 
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) IV, the State/UT 
Governments update the District Rural Roads Plan (DRRP) and 
generate the Comprehensive New Connectivity Priority List (CNCPL) 
of the unconnected habitations keeping in view, inter-alia, the 
suggestions received from Hon'ble Members of Parliament. The unit 
for connectivity under PMGSY IV is unconnected habitation. Shiridi 
pilgrimage site falls in Ahilyanagar district.  As per the Gram Sadak 
Survey (GSS) conducted by the State Government of Maharashtra

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1477. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
FDI TARGETS 
1477.  SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has any proposal to reform its policies to achieve the 
annual Foreign Director Investment (FDI) target of 100 billion dollars; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  the reasons for FDI reaching lowest in financial year 2024 and the steps being 
taken by  the Government to prevent this trend, during the last five financial 
years; 
 
(d)  the progress made by the Government in liberalising FDI  in sensitive sectors 
such as defence and insurance and telecommunications along with their impact 
on FDI in 2024; 
 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to attract investments in the services, 
software and manufacturing sectors; and 
 
(f)  the timeline fi xed by the Government for achieving the FDI target and the 
mechanisms placed to monitor its progress? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (f): The Government reviews the FDI policy on an ongoing basis and makes 
significant changes from time to time, to ensure that India remains an attractive 
& investor -friendly destination. The steps taken to attract larger FDI include 
removing regulatory barriers, streamlining processes, developing 
infrastructure, bettering logistics and improving the business environment by 
enhancing the Ease of Doing Business (EoDB). 
The Government does not fix targets for FDI inflows as FDI is largely a matter 
of private business decisions. FDI inflows depend on a host of factors such as 
availability of natural resources, market size, infrastructure, political and 
general investment climate, as well as macroeconomic stability and investment 
decisions of foreign investors. 

The Government has undertaken significant reforms across multiple sectors to 
liberalise FDI policy. FDI policy provisions have been progressively liberalised 
and simplified across various sectors such as Pension, Other Financial 
Services, Asset reconstruct ion Companies, Broadcasting, Pharmaceuticals, 
Single Brand Retail Trading, Construction & Development, Power Exchanges, 
e-commerce activities, Coal Mining, Contract Manufacturing, Digital Media, 
Civil Aviation etc. In the recent past, reforms in the FDI Po licy have been 
undertaken in sectors such as Defence, Insurance, Petroleum & Natural Gas, 
Telecom and Space. Specifically, the FDI Policy was amended vide Press Note 
No. 4 (2020 series), to allow FDI up to 74% through the Automatic Route for 
companies seeking a new defence industrial license, and up to 100% through 
the Government Route wherever it is likely to result in access to modern 
technology. Similarly, the FDI policy for insurance companies was amended 
vide Press Note 1 (2026 series) to increase the FDI limit from 74% to 100%. 
This enhanced limit is expected to attract long-term institutional capital, improve 
insurance penetration, and strengthen financial resilience. Furthermore, the 
FDI Policy in the Telecom sector was amended vide Press note 4 (2021) Series 
to allow 100% FDI under the automatic route for telecom services. 
To complement the reforms,  eﬀorts have been undertaken to ensure a 
seamless business regulatory framework across the country and nudge states 
to promote healthy competition to attract investments. The Government of India 
released Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) 2024 rankings and Logistics 
Ease Across Diﬀerent  States (LEADS) 2024 report to inter-alia 
communicate to potential investors examples of positive business ecosystem 
as well as logistics performance undertaken by various States and UTs. Under 
the Regulatory Compliance Burden (RCB) excercise, 47,865 compliances 
reduced since 2020 out of which 16,136 simplified, 22,289 digitised, 5 ,170 
decriminalised, 4,270 redundancies rem oved. Through the Jan Vishwas 
(Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023, the Government has decriminalised 183 
provisions across 42 Central Acts from 19 Ministries/Departments. Building 
upon the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, the Government undertook a comprehensive 
review of central laws and introduced the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of 
Provisions) Act, 2026, which amends 784 provisions across 79 Central Acts 
administered by 23 Ministries. Of these, 717 provisions have been 
decriminalized to promote Ease of Doing Business, w hile 67 provisions have 
been amended to facilitate Ease of Living. All these have resulted in FDI inflow 
reported in the Financial Year 2025 -26 (USD 94.84 billion) being the highest 
ever for a financial year showing an increase of nearly 18% compared to th e 
previous FY 2024-25 (USD 80.62 billion). 
Various steps taken to attract investments in services, software, and the 
manufacturing sector are placed at Annexure. 
 
******** 
 

ANNEXURE 
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (f) OF THE LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1477 FOR ANSWER ON 28.07.2026. 
Steps taken to attract investments in services, software, and the manufacturing 
sector 
The details of steps taken to attract investments and improve India’s attractiveness as 
an investment destination, particularly in the Software, Service, and Manufacturing 
Sector, are placed below: 
1. Software Sector: 
To attract FDI in the software sector, Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and  Software 
Technology Parks of India (STPIs) have been set up to promote the growth o f the 
software sector by providing tax benefits, infrastructure support, and regulatory ease. 
SEZs oﬀer tax incentives, simplified regulations, and world -class infrastructure to 
attract foreign and domestic investments in IT and software development. Furth er, 
STPIs help to promote software development and exports in addition to Government-
backed incentives like Make in India and Digital India. Further, to facilitate the inflow 
of FDI and to build investors trust , Government has taken initiatives such as National 
Policy on Software Products , targeted PLI schemes, and an enhanced data protection 
framework. 
2. Service Sector: 
To address barriers in service sectors, concerted eﬀorts have been put to promote the 
Startup and Innovation Ecosystem in India. FDI inflows in the services sector rose by 
40.77% in FY 2024 –25, reaching US$ 9.35 billion, up from US$ 6.64 billion in the 
previous year. This sector accounted for 19% of total FDI equity inflows, making it the 
top recipient. 
To address barriers in service sectors, concerted eﬀorts have been put to promote the 
Startup and Innovation Ecosystem in India. FDI equity  inflows in the services sector  
rose by 40.77% in FY 2024–25, reaching US$ 9.35 billion, up from US$ 6.64 
billion in the previous year and accounted f or 19% of total FDI equity inflows, making 
it the top recipient. In the FY 2025 -26, FDI inflows was US $ 10.01 bn in  the service 
sectors and contributed to 17% of total FDI equity inflows. 
3. Manufacturing Sector: 
The Government has undertaken several initiatives to accelerate growth and establish 
India as a global manufacturing powerhouse. In order to attract investments, 100% FDI 
is allowed the automatic route in the Manufacturing sector. Some of the initiatives by 
the Government include: 
 PLI Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing 
 PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware 
 Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0) Scheme 

 Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and 
Semiconductors (SPECS) 
 Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) 
 Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order to promote using 
made in India goods 
 Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) 
These initiatives have enabled the creation of a conducive investment ecosystem, 
leading to substantial growth in production, exports, employment and value 
addition in the electronics manufacturing sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1478 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
 
IMPACT OF E20 FUEL ON VEHICLES 
 
1478. ADV PRIYA SAROJ:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any independent study on the impact of E20 fuel on 
engine performance, fuel efficiency and maintenance costs of vehicles manufactured before the 
introduction of E20-compatible engines;  
 
(b) the details of number of  complaints received from consumers regarding mileage reduction, 
engine damage or component failure allegedly linked to E20 fuel, State-wise;  
 
(c) whether any automobile manufacturers have reported technical concerns regarding the use of 
E20 in older vehicles and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the additional financial burden on vehicle owners due to 
modifications, repairs or reduced fuel efficiency arising from E20 adoption; and  
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to issue any advisory, compensation mechanism or transition 
support for owners of non-E20-compatible vehicles? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a): An Inter -Ministerial Committee (IMC), constituted on 26 December , 2020 under NITI 
Aayog, comprehensively examined vehicle compatibility and mileage/efficiency aspects of 
ethanol blending. This assessment was supported by research conducted by Indian Oil Corporation 
Ltd. (IOCL), the Automotive Research Associ ation of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian 
Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM). Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by 
ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile manufacturers covering engine durability, drivability, 
cold startability, corro sion resistance, material compatibility, fuel system reliability, emissions 
performance and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed 
standards. Automobile manufacturers, component suppliers, SIAM, ARAI, testing agencies and 
Oil Marketing Companies were associated with every stage of the scientific evaluation and phased 
rollout of E20. E20 was introduced only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine 
durability, drivability, material compatibility and emissions perfo rmance. These studies did not 
reveal any significant adverse impact on performance, durability or material compatibility in 
legacy vehicles under the prescribed operating conditions. 
 
(b): No such data is compiled by MHI. 
 
(c): No such technical concerns have been reported to MHI by automobile manufacturers. 
 
(d): MHI has not done any such assessment. 
 
(e): There is no such proposal under consideration of MHI.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1479 
  ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
 
ROAD PROJECTS FOR BIHAR UNDER PMGSY 
 
1479. Smt. Lovely Anand: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has launched the Pradhan Mantri Gram 
Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Phase-IV for the financial years 2024-29, 
State-wise including Bihar; 
(b)  whether Bihar has been accorded priority under the schme in 
view of its large rural population and road connetivity 
requirment, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  the details of the number of eligible rural habitations, number of 
eligible projects, number of road proposals received from the 
State Government and number of projects approved so far for 
Bihar under PMGSY, district-wise; 
(d)  the details and the number of eligible rural habitations, eligible 
projects, road proposals received from the State Government, 
approved projects, approved road length, approved amount and 
the current progress of the projects, district-wise including 
Sheohar; and 
(e)  whether eligible project has not been approved by the 
Government, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor along with the timeframe for their approval? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): The Union Cabinet approved Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak 
Yojana-IV (PMGSY-IV), for implementation during FY 2024–25 to FY 
2028–29 with the target to provide all-weather road connectivity 
(construction of 62,500 km of roads) to 25,000 eligible unconnected 
habitations across the country with a total outlay of Rs.70,125 crore. 
There is no state-wise target under PMGSY-IV. The eligibility criteria 

Page 2 of 3 
 
of the habitations to be provided connectivity under PMGSY-IV based 
on population norms of Census 2011 are as follows: 
i. Habitations with a population of 500 and above in plains,  
ii. Habitations with a population of 250 and above in Special 
Category States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Ladakh, Manipur, 
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Himachal 
Pradesh, Jammu Kashmir and Uttarakhand), Special Category 
Areas [Tribal Schedule-V Areas, Desert Areas, Aspirational 
Blocks/ Districts and Hilly areas as notified by the respective 
State Government (cross slope more than 25% gradient and the 
elevation is more than 600 metres from the Mean Sea Level)] 
and  
iii. Habitations with a population of 100 and above in LWE affected 
Districts including Legacy & Thrust Districts identified by MHA 
from time to time. 
 
(c) & (d): The identification of eligible habitations, preparation of 
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), and submission of proposals are 
undertaken by the State Government through the State Rural Roads 
Development Agency (SRRDA) using the Online Management, 
Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS). 
Across all phases of PMGSY (PMGSY-I, II, III, and RCPLWEA), a 
total of 18,764 roads measuring 65,584 km and 2,085 bridges have 
been sanctioned in the State of Bihar, out of which 62,724 km of road 
length and 1821 bridges have been completed till date, connecting 
31,293 habitations. The details of works sanctioned and completed 
under all verticals of PMGSY in the State of Bihar including District-
wise details including that of Sheohar district are available in the 
public domain via the Online Management, Monitoring and 
Accounting System (OMMAS) portal and may be seen at 
https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb. 
 
(e): Clearance of road proposals under PMGSY is an ongoing 
process governed by programme guidelines. Projects are sanctioned 
based on the following standard procedure: 
i. Submission on OMMAS: The State Government prepares DPRs and 
uploads vetted proposals on the OMMAS portal. 
ii. Technical Scrutiny: DPRs are scrutinised by State Technical 
Agencies (STAs), Principal Technical Agencies (PTAs) and National 
Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA). 
iii. Empowered Committee Consideration: Eligible proposals are 
placed before the Inter-Ministerial Empowered Committee (EC) of the 
Ministry of Rural Development for consideration. 
Proposals are deferred or not approved primarily due to: 

Page 3 of 3 
 
 Incomplete Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) or pending 
information sought from the State Government regarding them.  
 Issues related to land availability or alignment disputes. 
  
Once the State Government resolves technical queries and 
submits fully compliant proposals, they are considered for approval 
by the Empowered Committee in a time-bound manner. As on date, 
under PMGSY-IV, the State of Bihar has uploaded 20 nos of road 
works for a length of 22.83 km covering 21 nos of habitations and 4 
bridges on Programme MIS of PMGSY which are under scrutiny.  No 
other proposal is pending for sanction.

1480.   Shri Rajesh Naranbhai Chudasama: 
Shri Mahesh Kashyap: 
Shri Dileshwar Kamait: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
(a)   the various objectives, key components and implementation framework of the initiative 
for the integrated development of 500 res ervoirs and Amrit Sarovars announced in the 
Union Budget 2026-27, State-wise and the manner in which Chhattisgarh particularly the 
Lok Sabha Constituency of Bastar in Chhattisgarh has been included in this initiative; 
(b)   the status and criteria of identification of reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars for implementation 
of the initiative in the country, State-wise including Bihar; 
(c)  the number of reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars identified under this initiative, State -wise 
including Chhattisgarh and Lok Sabha Constituency of Bastar and the criteria fixed for 
their selection, district-wise; 
(d)  the manner in which Chhattisgarh has been included in the initiative particularly Lok Sabha 
Constituency Bastar in Chhattisgarh; 
(e)  the proposed coverage of Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (Fish FPOs), women -led 
groups and fisheries cooperatives and individual beneficiaries associated with fish 
cultivation included/proposed to be included under the said initiative in the country, State-
wise including district -wise in Chhattisgarh and Lok Sabha Constituency Bastar in 
Chhattisgarh; and 
(f) the planned investment including the contribution of the Centre and the State for 
implementation of the initiative and if so, the details thereof State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a): The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026 -27 has announced the development 
of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and 
Amrit Sarovars in the country  including Bastar  constituency in Chhattisgarh. The initiative 
reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from 
reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihood s of fishermen in the reservoirs and 
engagement of women self-help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer 
Organizations (FFPO) for the development of fisheries in Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. The 

key components of this initiative  includes strengthening quality seed production by 
establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets 
to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the 
Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice 
plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value addition units.  
(b) to (d): The selection of the Reservoirs and Amrit sarovars  by the  Department of Fisheries 
(DoF), Government of India (GoI) has been done in consultation with States and Union 
Territories (UTs), considering the perennial water availability  and fisheries potential of the 
identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. Accordingly, 12 number of reservoirs and 5 numbers 
of Amrit Sarovars from Bihar and 27 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars from Chhattisgarh  
including Kosardeda reservoir from Bastar Constituency has been selected . District-wise 
reservoir selected in Chhattisgarh in consultation with the State Government is at Annexure -
III.   
(e) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying 
(MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the  objective of enhancing fishers’ income in 
the country is promoting involvement of Fish Farmer Producer Organization s (FFPOs), 
women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs 
and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of Fish F armer Producer Organizations 
(FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, 
in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. 
(f) The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs a nd 
Amrit Sarovars is to be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the Sta tes 
and Union Territories (UTs). T he  unit cost and funding pattern are as per the existing 
guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1482. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 28TH JULY, 2026. 
 
CGSS IN RAJASTHAN 
 
1482.  SHRI UMMEDA RAM BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the number of startups that have availed benefits under the Credit Guarantee 
Scheme for Startups (CGSS) in Rajasthan, including Barmer district, since the 
inception of the Scheme; 
 
(b)  the details of credit guarantees approved and the amount of credit extended 
under the Scheme in Rajasthan during the said period; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of Scheme in 
Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof, district -wise including Barmer district; 
and 
 
(d)  the measures taken by the Government to improve access to credit for startups 
under the Scheme in Rajasthan, particularly in Barmer district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (c): The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) is implemented for 
enabling debt funding to startups through eligible financial institutions [Member 
Institutions (MIs)]. CGSS is operationalized by the National Credit Guarantee 
Trustee Company (NCGTC) Limit ed and has been operationalized from 1st 
April 2023. The CGSS is implemented across the country, including in the State 
of Rajasthan. 
Specifically, in the State of Rajasthan 6 loans amounting to Rs 28.10 crore have 
been guaranteed to startup borrowers from Jaipur and Udaipur as on 30th June 
2026. 
The Management Committee (MC) constituted under the Scheme is 
responsible for reviewing, supervising and monitoring the functioning of the 
Scheme and is empowered to appraise its performance. Further, the MIs 
evaluate credit proposals based on prudent banking judgement and undertake 
due diligence while sanctioning and monitoring loans in accordance with the 

operational guidelines of the Scheme. The Scheme guidelines are available 
online at: 
https://www.ncgtc.in//content/products/0/20250509/Gazette_Notification_CGSS
_8th_May_2025_44e1a2d0dc.pdf 
(d): The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and 
NCGTC regularly engage with startups and Member Institutions (MIs) to review 
the implementation of the Scheme, address operational issues, discuss 
progress and facilitate greater participation of lenders and uptake of the 
Scheme. In addition, the Management Co mmittee periodically reviews the 
functioning and performance of the Scheme. 
Based on stakeholder discussions and fe edback, the Government expanded 
the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) vide notification dated 8 th  
May 2025 by increasing the ceiling on guarantee cover per borrower from Rs. 
10 crore to Rs. 20 crore, enhancing guarantee coverage to 85% of the amount 
in default for loans up to Rs. 10 crore and 75% for loans above Rs. 10 crore, as 
well as reducing the Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) to 1% for lenders supporting 
startups in 27 Champion Sectors, and introducing operational reforms for wider 
coverage of eligible startups. 
The Government has undertaken several measures to improve awareness, 
simplify access and enhanc e credit flow to startups across the country, 
including in the State of Rajasthan: 
i. Launch of the Startup Common Application Journey on the Jan Samarth 
Portal, providing a unified digital platform for startups to apply for loans and 
track their application. 
ii. Organization of awareness and outreach programmes by DPIIT in 
collaboration with NCGTC across various cities bringing together startups 
and MIs to improve awareness and facilitate access to credit. 
iii. Regular interactions with the leadership of MIs to address implementation 
issues, review progress and facilitate improved credit flow under the 
Scheme. 
 
As a result of such initiatives, the number and value of guarantees under the 
Scheme have witnessed significant growth. As on 30th June 2026, 478 loans 
amounting to approximately Rs. 1,469.92 crore have been guaranteed under 
the Scheme, of which more than Rs. 660 crore has been guaranteed during 
2026 (up to 30th June 2026).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1484 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 28TH JULY, 2026/ SHRAVANA 6, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
CYBER FINANCIAL FRAUD 
 
†1484.      SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the Government can state the reasons for registering no drop in the cases 
of cyber financial fraud despite the achievements of 14C; 
 
(b) whether  the Government has maintained any data regarding that has 
actually been refunded to the victims out of the total amount involved in the 
reported fraud cases; 
 
(c) the number of chargesheets filed so far against organised gangs involved 
in mule accounts and fake SIM cards; 
 
(d) whether the Government admits that negligence on the part of Telecom 
Service Providers is also a major cause of cyber frauds; and 
 
(e) if so, the details of the action taken against such operators? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (e) : ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the States and Union 
Territories (UTs) are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, 
investigation, and prosecution of cybercrime including cyber financial fraud.  

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 1484 FOR 28.07.2026  
The Central Government, through the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), 
supplements the efforts of States and UTs by providing policy guidance, 
technological support, capacity-building assistance, and financial resources 
to strengthen cybercrime management and enforcement capabilities.  
 
The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and publishes the 
statistical data on crimes in its publication “Crime in India”. The latest 
published report is for the year 2024.  Data regarding chargesheets filed 
against organised gangs involved in mule accounts and fake SIM cards is not 
maintained by NCRB.  
 
The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has  been launched in year 2021 for immediate 
reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. 
As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more 
than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.   
 
A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched 
by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 
30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspe ct identifier data received from 
Banks  and  32.08  lakh  Layer 1  mule  accounts  have  been  shared with the  
 

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 1484 FOR 28.07.2026  
participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth 
Rs. 25,698 crores. Till 30.06.2026, more than 15.75 lakhs SIM cards and 5.77 
lakhs IMEIs as reported by Police authorities have been blocked by 
Government of India. 
 
Department of Telecommunications  (DoT) undertakes efforts to 
prevent misuse of telecom resources in cyber -frauds. Sanchar Saathi portal 
and mobile app enables citizens to report the suspected fraud 
communications. Rather than acting on individual reported suspected fraud 
communications, DoT uses the crowd-sourced data to carry out analysis and 
to zero down on misuse of telecom resources. As on 15.7.2026, based on 
11.18 lakh reports of suspected fraud communication shared by citizens on 
Sanchar Saathi, 50.90 lakh mobile connections have been disconnected after 
failing reverification by Telecom Service Providers.

MEETING OF STATE LEVEL GUIDELINES COMMITTEE 
 
1485. Shri Sudhakar Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details and number of meetings of the State Level Guidelines 
Committee held in the State of Bihar during the last five years, 
year-wise; 
(b)  the major decisions taken and guidelines issued regarding the 
development of the State; and 
(c)  whether the Government has  any mechanism to ensure regular 
meetings of the State Level Guidelines Committee  and to 
ensure implementation of decisions made in the meetings in a 
time-bound manner? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
(a) to (c): State Level Guidelines Committees are not constituted 
by the Ministry of Rural Development in the State. 
However, the Ministry of Rural Development constitutes District 
Level Development Coordination and Monitoring Committees (DISHA) 
under the chairpersonship of the respective Members of Parliament 
to foster better coordination among elected representatives of 
Parliament, State Legislatures, and Local Governments (Panchayati 
Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies), and to ensure the effective 
and timely implementation of key Central Sector and Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes at the district level. To address unresolved 
issues and directions emerging from the District Level DISHA 
Committee (DLDC) meetings that require intervention at a higher 
level, the respective States/Union Territories constitute State Level 
DISHA Committees (SLDC) under the chairpersonship of the 

Page 2 of 2 
 
respective Chief Ministers or Lieutenant Governors to provide 
necessary guidance and facilitate resolution. 
As per the information available, 130 District Level DISHA 
Committee meetings have been convened in various districts of Bihar 
till date after the reconstitution of the DLDCs on 8 August 2024. 
However, the SLDC has not yet been constituted by the State 
Government. 
Recognizing the critical importance of DISHA, the Ministry of 
Rural Development (MoRD) is persistently working to ensure that 
State Level DISHA Committees are constituted in all the States/UTs 
and that their meetings are convened on a regular basis. Recently, 
vide letter dated 03.07.2026, all States/UTs including Bihar, were 
reminded to take necessary steps to constitute the State Level 
DISHA Committee and convene its meetings regularly in accordance 
with the provisions of the DISHA Guidelines.

  In so far as the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika

IMPLEMENTATION OF TEXTILE SCHEMES IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
 
1487.  SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the  details of schemes implemented by the Ministry during the last three years in Andhra 
Pradesh especially in Konaseema district, scheme and district-wise;  
(b) the number of beneficiaries under the schemes and Pehchan Cards issued in Andhra Pradesh, 
scheme and district-wise especially in Konaseema district;  
(c) the details of textile clusters, handloom clusters, PM MITRA Parks, Common Facility 
Centres and other infrastructure sanctioned or operational in Andhra Pradesh, district-wise;  
(d) the details of skill development programmes under the Government during the said period, 
including persons trained and placed, district -wise, especially in Konaseema district of Andhra 
Pradesh;  
(e) the details of marketing support, e -commerce linkage and credit or interest subvention 
extended to textile stakeholders in Andhra Pradesh, district-wise;  
(f) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under textile schemes in Andhra Pradesh 
during the last three years, scheme-wise and district-wise; and  
(g) the details of steps taken and proposed to strengthen the textile and handloom sector in 
Andhra Pradesh, particularly in Konaseema district? 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री(श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (g):     The Government of India has implemented various schemes/initiatives for textile sector 
across the country including Andhra Pradesh. The major schemes/ initiatives include Production 
Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme focusing on Man -Made Fibre (MMF) Fabric, MMF Apparel and 
Technical Textiles to boost large scale manufacturing and enhancing competitiveness; PM Mega 
Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks; Scheme for Integrated Textile Park 
(SITP) to provide subsidy for setting up textile parks; National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) 
focusing on Research and Innovation in the field of specialty fibres and   technical textiles, 
indigenous development of machinery and creating human resources with requisit e skills;   Silk 
Samagra-2 for the overall development of the silk industry; SAMARTH -Scheme for Capacity 
Building in Textile Sector with the objective of providing demand driven, placement oriented, 
skilling program; National Handloom Development Programme;  Raw Material Supply Scheme 
(RMSS) and National Handicraft Development Programme. 
  

During last three years and current year, the following support has been provided under Handloom 
sector in Andhra Pradesh: 
i. 22 Small Handloom Clusters have been taken up for  financial assistance of Rs.16.35 crore, 
benefitting 4,000 handloom workers 
ii. One Mega Handloom Cluster has been taken up at Dharmavaram (Andhra Pradesh 2025-26). 
iii. 14 marketing events were organised to facilitate and promote sales of Handloom Products. 
iv. 40 Handloom Producer companies have been formed to enhance productivity, marketing 
capabilities and facilitate better incomes. 
v. 5,987 beneficiaries were provided loans under Weavers’ MUDRA Scheme 
vi. 9,408 beneficiaries were enrolled under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jy oti Bima Yojana and 
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana.  
vii. Total 22.34 lakh kg of yarn has been supplied under Transport Subsidy & Price Subsidy 
benefitting more than 69,973 handloom organisations/weavers.  
viii. Pehchan cards have been issued to 1,77,447 handloom workers in Andhra Pradesh.  
  
The details of handloom clusters financially assisted under National Handloom Development 
Programme during last three years in Andhra Pradesh are at Annexure. Further, need -based skill 
upgradation training is conducted for h andloom workers/weavers across the country including 
Andhra Pradesh. Skill training has been imparted to 771 handloom weavers of Andhra Pradesh 
during the last three years. An e -commerce portal (https://www.indiahandmade.com/) has been 
launched to support weavers and artisans for online marketing of handloom products. In addition, 
handloom weavers were onboarded on Government e -Market place to enable them to sell their 
products directly to various Government Departments and organizations. 
  
  
Under National Handicraft Development Programme, 840 Pehchan Cards have been issued and 192 
artisans have been benefited and 4 Skill Development Programmes were conducted, benefiting 140 
artisans, during the last three years in Konaseema District, Andhra Pradesh. 
  
Under SAMARTH scheme, a total of 11852 beneficiaries were trained (Passed) and a total of 9582 
beneficiaries were placed in the State of Andhra Pradesh during the last three years. 
Under SITP Scheme, 4 Textile parks have been approved in Andhra Pradesh, namely  Brandix India

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 1489 
ANSWERED ON 28.07.2026 
  
GIS-BASED MAPPING 
 
  
1489. SHRI DHAVAL LAXMANBHAI PATEL: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  the details of the progress made in geo-tagging and GIS-based mapping of Gram 
Panchayat assets under the Panchayat-level GIS initiative in Valsad Parliamentary Constituency; 
  
(b)  whether the geo-spatial data generated under the initiative has been integrated with the 
PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan or any other national planning platform, if so, the details 
thereof; and  
  
(c)  if so, the manner in which such GIS-based planning has improved infrastructure 
planning, convergence of schemes and service delivery in tribal and remote Gram Panchayats? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a)   Under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), the Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
has developed the mActionSoft mobile application, which is integrated with the eGramSwaraj 
portal since 2020–21 to facilitate geo-tagging and monitoring of assets and works undertaken by 
Gram Panchayats. The application enables geo-tagging of assets at three stages of execution, 
namely before commencement, during progress and upon completion, thereby promoting 
transparency, accountability and effective monitoring.  
A total of 3,232 assets have been geo-tagged across Gram Panchayats in the Valsad 
Parliamentary Constituency during the year 2025-26. 
(b)  Yes Sir. Geo-tagged data of assets created and maintained under the Finance Commission 
Grants has been integrated with the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (NMP). The data has 
also been integrated with the Gram Manchitra platform for the purpose of more effective Gram 
Panchayat Development Planning (GPDP).  
(c) The integration of GIS-based information enables Gram Panchayats to access location-
specific information on public assets, identify infrastructure gaps, and undertake need-based 
planning at the local level. It also facilitates planning of development works with due 

2 
 
consideration to existing infrastructure and promotes convergence of activities under various 
Central and State Government schemes during the GPDP preparation process.  
With regards to tribal and remote Gram Panchayats, the availability of geo-tagged asset 
information and spatial mapping facilitates planning and prioritization of works relating to rural 
connectivity, drinking water sources, schools, health facilities, Anganwadi Centres, community 
assets and other basic infrastructure based on local requirements. It  also assists Gram 
Panchayats in identifying underserved habitations, assessing infrastructure gaps, avoiding 
duplication of assets and preparing need-based Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) 
through informed local planning.

(a): Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural

 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 1491

SHRI NARAYAN TATU RANE: 
SHRI RAJPALSINH MAHENDRASINH JADAV: 
SHRI MURASOLI S: 
SHRI ASHOK KUMAR RAWAT: 
DR. C M RAMESH: 
SHRI HARIBHAI PATEL: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  the details and status of implementation of e-Gram Swaraj and Audit Online across Gram 
Panchayats, State-wise; 
  
(b)  the status of preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and the current 
status of integration of e-Gram Swaraj with other digital governance platforms for planning and 
financial management, State-wise; 
  
(c)  whether training programmes have been conducted for elected representatives 
and Panchayat officials under these platforms, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
  
(d)  the details of funds disbursed and pending for panchayats, district the Rashtriya 
Gram Swaraj Abhiyan during the last five years, State-wise including in Panchayat in Thanjavur 
district; 
  
(e)  the details and status of implementation of the e-Gram Swaraj portal for panchayats in

panchayat; 
  
(f)  whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the e-Gram Swaraj and

(g)  the number of Gram Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh and Anakapalli that have prepared 
and uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) through e-Gram Swaraj during

(h)  whether the Government proposes to integrate e-Gram Swaraj with other digital

and timeline, State-wise?

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a), (b), (e), (f) & (g)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat 
Mission Mode Project (MMP) to strengthen digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions 
across the country. Under the project, eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline have been developed to 
facilitate digital planning, budgeting, accounting, audit, asset management and monitoring of 
Panchayat activities. Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) are prepared through a 
participatory planning process and uploaded on the eGramSwaraj portal. The Ministry regularly 
reviews the implementation of these applications through periodic reviews, data analytics and 
technical support provided to the States/UTs. 
The State-wise details of implementation of eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, status of GPDP 
preparation during the last three years, implementation in Thanjavur district and Anakapalli Lok 
Sabha Constituency status are given at Annexure-I.

the planning, accounting, implementation, online payments, monitoring, and reporting of Gram 
Panchayat activities are carried out on a unified digital platform. 
  
eGramSwaraj has already been integrated with various Government digital platforms, including 
the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for online payments and financial 
management, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for procurement, BHASHINI for 
multilingual AI-enabled services, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for weather-
related information.

and capacity-building under the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) to facilitate

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1492 
ANSWERED ON 28/07/2026 
TRADITIONAL FISHERFOLK IN KERALA 
 
1492. Shri N K Premachandran: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES,  ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to ensure the livelihood of traditional fisherfolk in 
Kerala, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government examined the difficulties of fisherfolk in Kerala due to shortage of 
allocation of Kerosene to Kerala and if so, the steps taken by the Government to increase the 
allotment of kerosene to Kerala;  
(c) whether the Government has any proposals to increase the allotment of subsidised kerosene 
for the supply to fisherfolk for operating their outboard motor and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has evaluated the crisis of fisherfolk in Kerala due to reduction of 
allocation of kerosene in Kerala from 37056 KL from 2020-21 to 1854 KL; and 
(e) if so, the details of action taken by the Government to enhance the allotment of more 
subsidized kerosene for fisherfolk? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various 
schemes for holistic development of fisheries sector in all States/UTs including Kerala. The 
major schemes include Blue Revolution Scheme (2015-16 to 2019-20), extending Kisan Credit 
Card (KCC) to fisheries (since 2018-19), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development 
Fund (FIDF) (2018 -19 to 2025 -26), ‘Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana’ (PMMSY)’ 
(2020-21 to 2026-27), and a new Central Sector Sub-scheme viz. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan 
Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27). Enhancing fish production, ensuring 
sustainability of resources, strengthening of value chain, employment generation, safety & 
security of fishers and socio-economic wellbeing of fishers and fish farmers have been the core 
of these initiatives.  

 
During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026 -27) under PMMSY, DoF, GoI has 
accorded approvals to the fisheries development proposal of Government of Kerala amounting 
to Rs. 1413.91  crore. The approved activities inter-alia include livelihood support to fishers 
during fishing ban period, support to traditional fishers for procurement of boats and nets, 
establishment of integrated modern coastal fishing villages, establishment of clim ate resilient 
coastal fishing villages, additional and alternate livelihood activities such as bivalve cultivation, 
cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish markets & kiosks, cold chain facilities, live fish vending 
centres, need based training and skill d evelopment programmes and development of fishing 
harbours and marketing facilities etc.  
(b) to (e) The Central Government allocates Superior Kerosene Oil (SKO) on a quarterly basis, 
but its distribution within a State/UT under the Public Distribution System (PDS) is entirely 
managed by the respective State/UT Government. The Ministry of Petroleum & Natu ral Gas 
(MoP&NG) being the nodal Ministry on the subject matter has informed that a s kerosene is a 
polluting fuel and adversely impacts public health, the PDS Kerosene allocation to States/UTs 
including Kerala have been rationalized since 2010 -11. Till date, 21 States/UTs have become 
PDS Kerosene free. Government has formulated a new “PDS Kerosene Allocation Policy” for 
the period of 2025-26 to 2027-28 after stakeholders consultation including the Government of 
Kerala. As per the said Policy, the allocation is made to States/UTs under single category “PDS 
SKO” on quarterly basis for cooking & lighting and for special needs. Further, the State 
Governments have been given the liberty to sub -allocate PDS SKO for cooking and lighting or 
for special needs (fi sheries, mela, exhibitions, pandemic, calamity etc.) based on their specific 
requirement. Distribution of PDS SKO within State/UT under PDS network is carried out by 
concerned State/UT. Scale and Criteria of distribution is, accordingly, also decided by respective 
State/UT. 
MoPNG has further informed that under the new policy, the Government of Kerala has been 
allocated 22,704 KL PDS SKO for the year 2025-26 as against total allocation of 4,368 KL PDS 
SKO for the year 2024 -25 which reflects an increase of 4 19.78 %. During the FY 2025 -26 out 
of the allocated quantity of 22,704 KL the State uplifted 17,724 KL with a lapse of 4,980 KL.  
It is also informed that, in view of the prevailing geo -political situation an adhoc allocation of 
1716 KL PDS SKO was also ma de for cooking and lighting to the State vide MoPNG’s letter 
dated 12.03.2026 for upliftment till 30 th June 2026. Out of the allocated quantity, the state 
uplifted 1512 KL only lapsing 204 KL. Further, an allocation of 4068 KL/quarter has been made 
to the State of Kerala for Q1 (April-June, 2026) and Q2 (July-September, 2026), 2026-27.

MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE

MERCHANDISE TRADE DEFICIT IN INDIA 
  
1493.  SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA 
  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री) be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)  the details of India’s merchandise trade deficit during the last twenty years, including 
current year, year-wise; 
(b)  whether the Government considers the present level of merchandise trade deficit 
sustainable in view of India’s exports and imports and if so, the justification therefor; 
(c)  if not, the reasons for persistent trade deficit and the major factors contributing there to; 
and 
(d)  the steps taken by the Government to reduce trade deficit and promote self -reliance in 
domestic production to reduce import dependence? 
    
ANSWER 
  
वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
   
(a) India’s merchandise exports expanded nearly three -and-a-half times over the last twenty 
years, with exports rising to US $ 441.75 billion in FY 2025 -26 from US $ 126.41 billion in FY 
2006-07. Similarly, import also expanded due to increase in domestic demand and 
manufacturing capabilities from US$ 194.81 Bn to US$ 776.01 Bn in 2025-26.
