(b) and (c) India’s merchandise trade deficit must be understood within the broader context of 
its external sector and the structural features of a fast -growing, investment-driven economy. 
While the country has consistently recorded a merchandise trade deficit, India’s external sector 
remains resilient and sustainable, supported by strong services exports, robust remittance 
inflows, stable capital flows, and adequate foreign exchange reserves. 
The deficit primarily reflects the import requirements of a rapidly expanding economy rather 
than structural imbalances. A large share of India’s imports is productive in nature, directly 
contributing to domestic manufacturing capabilities, infrastructure creation, and export 
competitiveness. Key imports include crude oil, capital goods, electronic goods, machinery, 
fertilizers, and other intermediate inputs—all essential for manufacturing, industrial expansion, 
infrastructure development, and energy security. These imports enhance India’s p roductive 
capacity and long-term growth potential, rather than being consumption-driven liabilities. 
Thus, the merchandise trade deficit is best seen as a by-product of India’s development stage, 
investment needs, and energy dependence. Despite the deficit , the overall external sector 
remains stable, underpinned by strong fundamentals that ensure sustainability and resilience 
in the face of global uncertainties. 
At the same time, India's exports have demonstrated remarkable resilience despite a 
challenging global environment marked by geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, 
inflationary pressures and subdued external demand. India recorded highest -ever exports in 
FY 2025-26 reaching a record US$ 863.1 billion, with merchandise exports reaching US$ 441.8 
billion and services exports expanding further to US$ 421.3 Bn. The substantial surplus 
generated through services exports acts as an important buffer to the merchandise trade deficit 
and contributes significantly towards maintaining the sustainability of India's external sector. 
(d) The Government has adopted a comprehensive strategy aimed at achieving the twin 
objectives of reducing critical import dependence by strengthening domestic manufacturing 
capabilities while simultaneously expanding exports through improved competitiveness, 
market access and deeper integration with global value chains. 
To promote exports, the Government is implementing the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, 
which focuses on export diversification, market access, ease of doing business, digitalisation 
and integration into global value chains. India has also significantly expanded its trade 
engagement and currently has 19 active Free Trade Agreements, with eight major FTAs signed 
or concluded since 2021, providing enhanced preferential access to major global markets. 
Institutional initiatives such as the Export Promotion Mission, Districts as Export Hubs, Trade 
eConnect, the Trade Intelligence and Analytics (TIA) Portal, electronic Certificates of Origin, 

3 
 
and customs modernisation  are strengthening export competitiveness, improving market 
intelligence, facilitating compliance and enabling exporters, particularly MSMEs, to access new 
international markets. 
Simultaneously, the Government is strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities through 
improvements in infrastructure, logistics and the business ecosystem. Initiatives such as PM 
Gati Shakti National Master Plan, the National Logistics Policy, digitalisation of customs 
processes through SWIFT, and improvements in trade facili tation are reducing logistics costs 
and enhancing industrial competitiveness. 
To reduce strategic import dependence, the Government is also promoting domestic capacity 
creation in critical sectors, encouraging technology adoption and innovation, strengthen ing 
supply chain resilience, diversifying import sources for essential commodities such as crude 
oil, fertilisers and critical minerals, and accelerating investments in renewable energy and other 
emerging sectors. 
These measures are aimed at progressively improving India's export competitiveness, 
strengthening domestic production capabilities, reducing vulnerabilities arising from external 
shocks and ensuring sustainable long-term growth of the external sector.

1494: Shri Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer: 
Will the Minister of Cooperation (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the status of the current operational expansion status and driver (Sarathi) enrollment 
numbers of the Bharat Taxi Cooperative Mobility Platform since its launch; 
 
(b) the details of the structural and fair -pricing guardrails integrated into the platform’s 
architecture to permanently eliminate predatory surge pricing and protect urban commuters 
from monopolistic exploitation by private aggregators; and 
 
(c) the details of the financial outlays, equity grants, or technological subsidies provided 
through the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) to support the 
infrastructure scalability and long -term competitiveness of the Sahkar Taxi Cooperative 
Limited? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a)  Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi 
Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, registered under the MSCS Act 
2002. Bharat Taxi is providing its services in the cities of Delhi -NCR, Gujarat and Maharashtra. 
As on 19 July 2026, a total of 7.97 lakh Sarathis (driver-partners) have been onboarded under the 
cooperative-based Bharat Taxi initiative, all of whom have completed the document verification 
process. 
(b)  Bharat Taxi's fares are set on objective, pre -defined parameters, finalised in consultation 
with State Transport Authorities, Sarathi representatives and other stakeholders with no arbitrary 

Page 2 of 2 
 
or excessive surge pricing.  However, periodic congestions fare is applied due to excessive traffic, 
in line with the fair pricing acceptable to drivers and customers. 
 
(c)  Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) has been promoted by eight institutions, 
including the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). Each promoter has 
committed ₹10 crore towards the primary share capital of the Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Lim ited.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES 
(DIVYANGJAN) 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1495 
TO BE ANSWERED ON - 28/07/2026 
   
DIVYANG KALA SHAKTI 
  
1495 : Smt. Shambhavi; 
Dr. Lata Wankhede 
 
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that 90% of all Central Government buildings and major international 
airports have been made fully barrier-free as of July 2026, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the Ministry has successfully distributed the Unique Disability ID (UDID) cards 
to over 1 crore beneficiaries to ensure "one-nation-one-card" benefits, if so, the details thereof, 
State-wise: 
 
(c) whether the "Divyang Kala Shakti" initiative has successfully whether cased the artistic 
talents of divyangjans on international platforms to promote inclusivity, if so, the details 
thereof, State-wise; 
 
(d) whether the Ministry has provided interest-free loans to Divyangjan for setting up 
technology-driven small businesses through the NHFDC, if so, the details thereof, State-
wise;and  
 
(e) whether the new "National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation" has commenced its 
advanced clinical services for the community in the current quarter, if so, the details thereof? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
 (SHRI B. L. VERMA) 
  
(a):  Since, in terms of Sections 40, 41, 44 and 45 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 
Act, 2016, the appropriate Government is responsible for prescribing accessibility standards 
and taking necessary measures to ensure accessibility in the physical environment, 
transportation, information and communication, including appropriate technologies & systems, 
services and other facilities, the responsibility for implementation rests with the respective 
Central Ministries/Departments and State Governments/UT Administrations. Accordingly, 
data relating to the number of accessible Central Government buildings and major international 
airports is not maintained centrally by this Department. 
To facilitate the States/UTs, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities 
(DEPwD) implements an Umbrella Scheme- Scheme for Implementation of Rights of Persons 

2 
 
with Disabilities (SIPDA) Act, 2016 applicable across India. It has a component - “Scheme for 
Creation of Barrier Free Environment” (CBFE Scheme) through which financial assistance is 
provided to State/UT Governments on demand basis for creation of barrier free environment 
in existing government buildings and establishments as per receipt of compliant proposals. 
  
(b): The Unique Disability Identity (UDID) sub scheme is a flagship initiative of the 
Government of India. Under the UDID sub scheme, an online centralized platform namely 
UDID portal (https://swavlambancard.gov.in/) has been instituted where hospitals authorized 
by the respective State/UT Governments have been onboarded for issuance of disability 
certificates and Unique Disability Identity (UDID) cards to the eligible divyangjan. As on 
20.07.2026, 1.39 crores e-UDID cards have been issued across the country through the said 
portal by the hospitals authorized by State/UT Governments. and state-wise details has been 
attached at Annexure. 
(c): No dedicated international platform-specific programme has been undertaken under the 
Divyang Kala Shakti initiative. However, Divya Kala Shakti is a flagship national-level 
initiative of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry 
of Social Justice and Empowerment, aimed at promoting and showcasing the artistic talents of 
Divyangjan artists by providing them with a robust national platform, wider visibility, and 
opportunities for confidence-building. Since its inception, a total of 27 Divya Kala Shakti 
events have been organised across the country.  
(d): The National Handicapped Finance and Development Corporation (NHFDC) has been 
renamed as the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). 
NDFDC  is a Government enterprise dedicated to the economic and overall empowerment of 
Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) under the aegis of Department with an objective to provide 
concessional financial assistance for self-employment, education, and skill development of 
PwDs. However, presently, NDFDC does not provide interest-free loans to Divyangjan for 
setting up technology-driven small businesses. 
(e): The National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation (NIMHR), Sehore under this 
Department has commenced advanced clinical and rehabilitation services for the 
community.   The Institute is providing multidisciplinary mental health rehabilitation services 
through Psychiatry, Clinical Psychology, Psychiatric Social Work. Rehabilitation Psychology, 
Occupational Therapy, Special Education, Speech Therapy, Physiotherapy, and other 
rehabilitation disciplines. The services include OPD-based psychiatric consultation, 
comprehensive psychosocial and psychological assessment, individual and family counselling, 
psychosocial interventions, group therapy services, rehabilitation planning, disability 
certification facilitation, UDID support services, referral services, and community-based 
rehabilitation initiatives for persons with mental illness and persons with disabilities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1496 
FOR ANSWER ON 28.07.2026  
 
 
 
REVIEW OF PLI SCHEME FOR SPECIALTY STEEL 
 
 
 
1496.  SHRI K E PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Union Government has reviewed the participation of different States 
under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty Steel with reference 
to the geographical distribution of approved projects, investments and beneficiaries; 
 
(b) whether the Government has received any representations from industry bodies, 
steel manufacturers and MSMEs regarding greater location of beneficiary 
manufacturing facilities including Tamil Nadu, in the PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel 
and allied manufacturing sectors; 
 
(c) whether the Union Government proposes any measures to enhance participation 
of MSME-based steel and engineering units in industrial clusters of Tamil Nadu 
including Erode District where engineering and fabrication MSMEs operate under 
existing and future phases of the PLI Scheme; and 
 
(d) whether any policy initiatives are under consideration to promote wider regional 
dispersal of investments, value-added steel manufacturing and downstream industrial 
development through the PLI framework? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(d):   To participate in the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty 
Steel a company must be registered in India, commit to produce the specialty steel 
products by adhering to the investment and capacity thresholds, and have a net worth 
of at least 30 per cent of the committed investment. To facilitate wider participation 
from companies including MSMEs, eligibility criteria were relaxed in the third round of 
the scheme. 
The Scheme is applicable for all states in India. 167 projects of 100 companies 
from 15 States have been approved, which includes six projects in Tamil Nadu.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 1499 
ANSWERD ON 28TH JULY, 2026 
 
MOBILE VETERINARY UNITS 
 
1499.  SHRI ARUN BHARTI:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has effectively deployed Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) to provide 
doorstep medical care to livestock in the rural segments of Lok Sabha Constituency Jamui in Bihar; 
 (b) if so, the total number of centrally funded mobile veterinary vans currently operational and actively 
serving farmers in the constituency as of June 2026;  
(c) whether these units are fully equipped with necessary diagnostic equipment, surgical facilities, and 
essential medicines to handle complex rural veterinary emergencies, if so, the details thereof;  
(d) the details of the centralized toll-free helpline system established to allow farmers to rapidly request 
medical assistance for their ailing cattle; and  
(e) the steps proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure the timely recruitment and retention of 
qualified veterinary surgeons and support staff to man these mobile units efficiently?  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) and (b) Out of total 307 MVUs provided to the State of Bihar under Livestock Health & Disease 
Control Program (LHDCP) of the Department of A nimal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), 06 MVUs 
have been deployed in Jamui constituency to provide Veterinary care at farmer’s doors step.  
(c) The MVUs are equipped with necessary equipment for disease diagnosis, minor surgical 
interventions and essential medicines to handle Veterinary emergencies. 
 
(d) Centralized call centre s in the States are  having executives and Veterinary Doctor s to provide 
veterinary assistance services on call. Farmer’s can avail this facility by dialing toll free helpline number 
1962. 
 
(e) DAHD, GOI, under LHDCP Scheme, provides budgetary support to the States on sharing basis  to 
deploy Veterinarian, Para-Veterinarian and Driver-cum-attendant for MVUs. In this regard the physical 
and financial progress of the State is also monitored periodically.
